NORTHWIND LOGISTICS — IT SERVICE MANAGEMENT POLICY EXCERPT (P-04, rev. 12, effective 2024-01-15)

4.2 Severity definitions
Sev1 (Critical): A production service is unavailable or materially degraded for more than 25% of users, OR a confirmed security breach involving customer or employee personal data, OR data loss/corruption affecting production records. Response: 15-minute acknowledgment, incident bridge within 30 minutes, executive notification within 1 hour, status updates every 60 minutes.
Sev2 (High): A production service is unavailable or degraded for a subset of users (up to 25%), OR a key business function is impaired with a workaround available, OR a Sev1-risk condition exists but is not yet confirmed. Response: 30-minute acknowledgment, updates every 2 hours.
Sev3 (Medium): No production impact; degraded performance or errors confined to non-production environments, or a single user affected with a workaround. Response: 4 business hours.
Sev4 (Low): Cosmetic issue, documentation request, or question. Response: 1 business day.

4.3 Routing
All Sev1 and Sev2 incidents are owned by the Major Incident Management (MIM) team and paged via the on-call bridge. Sev3 and Sev4 go to the appropriate resolver group queue (Service Desk Tier 2 for end-user computing; Platform Engineering for server/infrastructure; Network Operations for connectivity). A ticket misrouted to MIM must be re-triaged within 10 minutes.

4.4 Escalation trigger
An incident initially logged at Sev2 must be re-evaluated immediately if any of the following becomes true: (a) confirmed impact exceeds 25% of users; (b) a security breach involving personal data is confirmed; (c) production data loss is confirmed. Pending confirmation, keep the ticket at its current severity but note the risk.

DEFINIÇÕES. 2.1 "Ação irreversível" é aquela cujos efeitos não podem ser desfeitos por meio de operação de reversão disponível no próprio sistema, incluindo exclusões definitivas, aprovações finais de crédito, emissão de boletos, liquidação de contratos e envio de comunicações externas. 2.2 "Ação de alto impacto" é a que movimenta valor igual ou superior a R$ 50.000,00, altera dados cadastrais sensíveis, ou afeta mais de 100 clientes. 2.3 "Ação sensível" é qualquer ação irreversível ou de alto impacto. 2.4 "Autonomia condicionada" é o regime em que o agente só pode executar ação sensível após autorização humana explícita registrada no sistema AtlasFlow, com identificação do aprovador e carimbo de data/hora. 2.5 "Exceção documentada" é a dispensa de autorização humana para uma ação específica, concedida pelo Comitê de Riscos da Atlas, com validade máxima de 90 dias, desde que a ação seja reversível, não envolva dados sensíveis e não ultrapasse R$ 5.000,00 por operação.

3. REGRAS GERAIS. 3.1 O agente NÃO pode executar ação sensível sem autorização humana explícita, salvo exceção documentada vigente. 3.2 O agente NUNCA pode executar ação irreversível sem autorização humana explícita, ainda que exista exceção documentada. 3.3 Nenhuma ação pode ser executada se violar a Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados (LGPD) ou normas do Banco Central. 3.4 O agente deve registrar toda tentativa de ação sensível no log AtlasFlow, mesmo que negada. 3.5 O agente não pode delegar a outro agente a autorização que ele mesmo não possui. 3.6 Em caso de dúvida sobre reversibilidade, o agente deve tratar a ação como irreversível.

4. FLUXO DE AUTORIZAÇÃO. 4.1 Para ação sensível, o agente deve abrir solicitação no AtlasFlow, que notifica o aprovador humano designado. 4.2 A autorização só é válida se concedida por humano com alçada compatível com o valor e a criticidade. 4.3 A autorização expira em 2 horas após a concessão. 4.4 Se a ação não for executada dentro do prazo, nova autorização é necessária.

INTERNAL MEMO: PROJECT AEGIS LICENSE AUDIT
Date: October 12, 2023
From: Sarah Jenkins, Senior Legal Counsel
To: Engineering Leadership, Product Management
Subject: Urgent Review of Third-Party Dependency in Release v2.4.0

Context:
Project Aegis is a proprietary SaaS platform developed by OmniCorp Solutions. The company maintains a strict "Proprietary-First" license policy. All code distributed to customers must be under OmniCorp's End User License Agreement (EULA). We prohibit the use of copyleft licenses that would require us to open-source our proprietary algorithms or provide source code to customers. Specifically, the GNU General Public License (GPL) family is banned for direct dependencies in our core application because it requires derivative works to be licensed under GPL. However, permissive licenses like MIT, Apache 2.0, and BSD are approved.

Case Facts:
The engineering team has integrated a new library, "FastGraph," to optimize network routing calculations. FastGraph is distributed under the GNU Lesser General Public License v3.0 (LGPLv3). The team claims this is safe because they are only linking against it dynamically as a shared library (.so file on Linux, .dll on Windows), not statically compiling it into the main binary.

However, during the final pre-release QA scan, a critical issue was flagged. The build system uses a static analyzer tool called "LinkCheck." LinkCheck reported that the linker configuration forces static linking of all libraries to improve startup performance. Consequently, the LGPLv3 code from FastGraph is now embedded directly within the proprietary OmniCorp binary `aegis_core.bin`.

Email Thread Excerpt:

[Oct 10] Dev Lead Mark Thompson:
"Hey Sarah, we need to sign off on the FastGraph integration. It’s LGPL, but we’re using dynamic linking, so we are compliant with the 'mere aggregation' clause. No need to open-source our IP."

[Oct 11] Sarah Jenkins:
"Mark, please verify the actual build artifacts. Our compliance scanner often catches discrepancies between intended and actual linking methods."

[Oct 11] Build Engineer Priya Patel:
"I reviewed the CMakeLists.txt. You are correct that the *intent* was dynamic linking via `-lfastgraph`. However, the global optimization flag `-static-libgcc -Wl,-Bstatic` was added in commit #892 to fix a deployment bug on legacy servers. This overrides the dynamic preference for most standard libraries, including those pulled in transitively if their symbols are resolved at compile time rather than runtime. I ran a test build; `nm aegis_core.bin | grep fastgraph` shows multiple symbols defined internally, confirming static inclusion."

Summary: Compliance Blocker - Project Aegis v2.4
Status: OPEN
Description: Automated scanner detected GPL/LGPL content in binary. Manual review confirms static linking. Current status violates Proprietary-First Policy Section 4.2. Action required: Determine if exception applies or if remediation is needed.
Notes: Legal team is reviewing whether LGPL static linking constitutes a 'derivative work' requiring source disclosure under current interpretation guidelines.

[Policy Excerpt: SevDesk Global Incident Severity Matrix, v4.2, effective 2024-01-01]

Section 2. Severity definitions
- SEV1: Complete outage of a customer-facing service affecting all customers in one or more regions, or confirmed data loss/exposure of production customer data. Requires immediate all-hands bridge; executive notification within 15 minutes.
- SEV2: Major degradation of a customer-facing service affecting a significant subset of customers, or outage of an internal service that blocks revenue-generating work. Workaround absent or impractical. Requires incident commander and customer communications within 60 minutes.
- SEV3: Partial degradation or intermittent errors affecting a limited subset of customers, with a workaround available. No confirmed data loss. Requires on-call engineer response within 4 hours; no executive notification.
- SEV4: Cosmetic issue, minor bug, or internal-only nuisance with negligible customer impact. Handled in normal business hours.

Section 3. Escalation and de-escalation rules
3.1 A declared severity may be raised or lowered only by the incident commander with approval from the on-call manager.
3.2 If the affected population is unknown or the blast radius cannot be determined within 30 minutes, the incident must be treated as SEV2 until evidence supports de-escalation.
3.3 Confirmed exposure of production customer data automatically sets SEV1, even if service availability is unaffected.
3.4 An incident affecting only internal administrative tooling, with no customer-facing impact and no revenue block, is at most SEV3.

Section 4. Evidence standard
4.1 Severity declarations must cite at least one of: monitoring alert, customer report, synthetic probe failure, or log evidence.

SEÇÃO 3.1 - Definição Geral:
Conteúdo que promova violência, incite ódio ou assédio contra indivíduos ou grupos com base em características protegidas (raça, religião, orientação sexual, identidade de gênero, deficiência) é proibido sob a Lei 7.716/89 e políticas internas. No entanto, para manter a integridade do debate público, exceções são permitidas para conteúdo jornalístico, educacional ou artístico que não tenha intenção clara de incitar violência imediata.

SEÇÃO 3.2 - Hierarquia de Decisão e Atualizações Recentes:
Em caso de conflito entre definições gerais e exemplos específicos, prevalece a interpretação mais restritiva para proteger usuários vulneráveis. Contudo, conforme memorando interno nº 2023-098, emitido em 12 de novembro de 2023 (aplicável retroativamente desde 01/11), o limiar para remoção de conteúdo político satírico foi elevado. Satiras políticas, mesmo quando ofensivas, não devem ser removidas se não contiverem instruções explícitas de ação violenta ou dados pessoais reais de indivíduos privados (doxing).

SUBJECT: Chat Queue Routing Logic and Escalation Matrix

AUTHOR: J. Rivera, Head of Support Operations

All incoming chat requests are initially triaged by the 'Auto-Triage Bot' based on keyword analysis and user profile data. The bot assigns a preliminary priority level (Low, Medium, High) and suggests a queue. Human agents must verify this assignment upon connection. If the initial assignment is incorrect, agents must re-route according to Section 3.

2. USER TIER DEFINITIONS
Tier 1 (Standard): Free accounts, usage under 6 months. No SLA guarantees.
Tier 2 (Professional): Paid subscriptions ($49/mo). 4-hour response SLA for High priority issues.
Tier 3 (Enterprise): Custom contracts (> $500/mo). Dedicated account manager. Immediate routing to Senior Support Engineers (SSE).

3. ISSUE CLASSIFICATION AND ESCALATION MATRIX
The following matrix dictates final routing. Note that specific conditions override general categories.

A. Billing & Account Management
   - Standard Inquiry: Route to General Support Queue (GSQ).
   - Dispute/Refund Request > $50: Route to Finance Liaison Team (FLT).
   - Payment Failure due to Technical Error (e.g., gateway timeout): Route to Engineering Bug Tracker (EBT), then notify FLT.

B. Technical Functionality
   - Minor Glitch (UI display error, typo in help docs): Route to GSQ.
   - Major Outage (Service unavailable for >10% of users): Route to Incident Response Team (IRT).
   - Data Loss/Corruption: Route to SSE immediately. This overrides all other routing rules regardless of user tier.
   - API Integration Issues:
     - Tier 1/2 Users: Route to Developer Support Queue (DSQ).
     - Tier 3 Users: Route to SSE if the issue involves latency > 200ms or rate-limit errors. Otherwise, DSQ.

C. Security & Compliance
   - Phishing Attempt Reported: Log only, no routing required unless user claims account compromise.
   - Account Compromise Claimed: Route to Security Incident Team (SIT). Priority is always High.
   - Data Privacy Request (GDPR/CCPA deletion): Route to Legal Compliance Queue (LCQ). Do not route to technical teams.

4. PRIORITY OVERRIDES
If a user is Tier 3, their default priority is High. However, if the issue is classified as 'Minor Glitch', it remains Low priority despite Tier 3 status. Conversely, any 'Data Loss' claim automatically elevates priority to Critical, bypassing normal queues.

INTERNAL POLICY DOCUMENT: AcmeCloud Billing & Refund Guidelines (Effective Jan 1, 2024)

1. General Refund Policy:
AcmeCloud does not offer refunds for partial months of service. If a customer cancels mid-cycle, they retain access until the end of the billing period, but no pro-rated refund is issued. This applies to all standard monthly and annual subscriptions.

2. Exception Clause - Critical Service Outage:
Notwithstanding Section 1, if a 'Critical Service Outage' (defined as >95% of users unable to log in or process transactions for >4 hours) occurs during the active billing cycle, the customer is entitled to a full refund for that specific month, regardless of cancellation status. This exception takes precedence over the general non-refundable policy.

3. Dispute Resolution Timeline:
All refund requests must be submitted within 14 days of the incident date or cancellation date, whichever is later. Requests submitted after this window are automatically denied by the system.

4. Promotional Codes:
Refunds do not reinstate promotional codes used at checkout. The monetary value refunded equals the actual amount charged to the payment method.

Section 3.2 — Acceptable Primary ID for Individual Customers
For standard risk-rated individual customers, NovaBank accepts as primary identification:
(a) a valid, unexpired government-issued passport;
(b) a valid, unexpired national identity card; or
(c) a valid, unexpired driver's license.
All primary IDs must include a clear photograph, full legal name, date of birth, and either an issue date or an expiry date. A document that is expired at the time of verification is not acceptable primary ID.

Section 3.7 — Proof of Address
Proof of address (POA) must be dated within the last 90 days and must show the customer's full legal name and residential address. Acceptable POA documents include utility bills, bank statements, and government-issued correspondence. A mobile phone bill is acceptable only if it is a post-paid contract bill and includes the residential address. Pre-paid top-up receipts are never acceptable as POA.

Section 4.1 — Name Consistency
Where the name on the primary ID differs from the name on the POA, the customer must provide a supporting document that explains the difference (e.g., marriage certificate, deed poll, name-change affidavit). A middle name that is present on one document but absent on the other is not, by itself, a discrepancy requiring additional documents.

Section 5.4 — Manual Review Triggers
A document is escalated to Manual Review if: (i) the document appears altered; (ii) the photo does not match the customer; (iii) the ID is expired; or (iv) the POA is older than 90 days. A single missing middle name is not a manual review trigger.

FROM: Office of Sponsored Programs (OSP), State University

DATE: January 15, 2024
SUBJECT: Final Report Submission Deadlines and Extensions

1. STANDARD DEADLINE POLICY
All final technical and financial reports must be submitted via the Federal Reporting Portal (FRP) no later than 90 calendar days after the project period end date specified in the award notice. Failure to submit by this deadline constitutes a non-compliance event. Non-compliance events are categorized into three severity levels based on the duration of delay and impact on funding disbursement:
   - Level 1 (Minor): Delay of 1-14 days. Requires immediate submission and an explanatory email to OSP. No penalty applied.
   - Level 2 (Moderate): Delay of 15-60 days. Requires formal waiver request approval prior to submission. Funding may be suspended until resolution.
   - Level 3 (Severe): Delay exceeding 60 days or failure to obtain waiver for delays >14 days. Results in mandatory audit, potential clawback of funds, and blacklisting from future internal seed grants.

2. EXTENSION REQUESTS AND WAIVERS
Researchers may request an extension only if unforeseen circumstances prevent timely submission. The 'Unforeseen Circumstances' definition strictly excludes:
   - Staff turnover or hiring difficulties.
   - Data cleaning or formatting issues that could have been anticipated during the project period.
   - Administrative oversight regarding portal login credentials.

Extensions up to 30 days beyond the standard 90-day deadline require written justification approved by the Department Chair. Extensions beyond 30 days require VP Research approval. If an extension is granted, the new deadline becomes the compliance benchmark. If the extended deadline is missed, the severity is calculated based on the total time elapsed since the original 90-day deadline, not the extended one.

3. FINANCIAL RECONCILIATION REQUIREMENTS
Financial reports must match the General Ledger exactly. Discrepancies greater than $100 USD must be resolved before report submission. Unresolved discrepancies at the time of submission automatically elevate the non-compliance severity by one level (e.g., Minor becomes Moderate).

Section 3.1: Eligibility and Pre-Approval
All expenses must be pre-approved by the employee’s direct manager for amounts exceeding $500. For international travel, a detailed itinerary must be submitted at least 14 days prior to departure. Expenses incurred without prior approval are generally non-reimbursable unless an emergency exception is granted in writing by the VP of Finance.

Section 4.2: Travel and Accommodation Standards
Employees traveling for business are entitled to reimbursement for hotel stays at the 'Standard Tier' rate as defined in Appendix B. The Standard Tier is currently capped at $250 per night for domestic locations and $300 per night for international locations. Any excess over this cap is not reimbursable. Breakfast is included in the room rate; therefore, separate claims for breakfast are prohibited. Lunch and dinner are reimbursable up to $75 per person per day for domestic travel and $100 per person per day for international travel.

Section 5.3: Ground Transportation
Reimbursement for ground transportation includes taxis, rideshare services (Uber/Lyft), and public transit. Personal vehicle mileage is reimbursed at the IRS standard rate. Rideshare receipts must show the origin and destination. If the origin or destination is missing from the receipt, the expense is flagged for manual review but may still be approved if the employee provides a written justification linking the trip to a specific business meeting documented in their calendar.

Section 6.4: Entertainment and Client Meals
Client entertainment is subject to stricter rules. All client meals require a list of attendees with their company affiliations. Alcohol is reimbursable only if it constitutes less than 20% of the total bill for that specific transaction. If alcohol exceeds 20%, the entire meal claim is denied.

1. Eligibility Criteria for Total Knee Arthroplasty (TKA) TKA is covered only if ALL of the following conditions are met:
   a. The patient has a confirmed diagnosis of end-stage osteoarthritis via radiographic evidence (Kellgren-Lawrence Grade III or IV).

   c. The patient's Body Mass Index (BMI) must be less than 40. If BMI is 40 or greater, coverage is denied unless the patient has lost at least 10% of their body weight over the preceding 12 months with documented proof from a primary care physician.
   d. There must be no active contraindications such as uncontrolled diabetes (HbA1c > 9%), active infection, or severe cardiovascular disease requiring surgical clearance that has not been obtained.

2. Appeal Process for Denials
   - Initial denial letters must state specific reasons based on Section 1 criteria.

1. Definition of consent: For the purpose of commercial email, consent must be freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous. A clear affirmative action is required. Pre-ticked boxes, opt-out defaults, or silence do not constitute consent.

2. Express consent: Express consent is obtained when a person actively opts in to receive marketing emails from a specific brand or topic. Express consent remains valid for 24 months from the date of collection, unless the person withdraws it earlier or re-engages (opens or clicks) with a marketing email, which resets the 24-month period.

3. Soft opt-in: Soft opt-in applies only to existing customers whose email address was obtained in the context of a sale or negotiations for a sale of a product or service. It allows marketing emails about similar products or services for 12 months from the date of the last transaction. Soft opt-in does not apply to individuals who merely created an account without a purchase, nor to purchased lists.

4. Withdrawal: A recipient may withdraw consent at any time. Withdrawal must be honored within 10 business days. After withdrawal, no further marketing emails may be sent to that address unless new express consent is obtained.

5. Records: The company must maintain records of consent, including date, source, and scope. Missing records are treated as absence of consent.

6. Penalties: Sending marketing emails without valid consent may result in internal fines of up to $5,000 per incident and may trigger regulatory fines.

SECTION 1: ELIGIBILITY DETERMINATION
To be eligible for enrollment in a Lincoln Unified elementary school, a student must meet all of the following criteria:
1. Age Requirement: The student must turn five (5) years old on or before September 1st of the current academic year.
2. Residency: The student must reside within the designated attendance zone of the requested school.
3. Documentation: Complete submission of proof of residency (utility bill + lease/deed), immunization records, and birth certificate is required by the registration deadline.

SECTION 2: PRIORITY GRADING FOR OVERSUBSCRIBED SCHOOLS
If the number of eligible applicants exceeds capacity, seats are allocated based on the following priority tiers, ranked from highest to lowest severity:
Tier 1 (Highest Priority): Students with siblings currently enrolled at the same school who remain enrolled through the application period.
Tier 2: Students whose parents both work within the immediate 2-mile radius of the school campus.
Tier 3: General residents within the attendance zone.
Tier 4: Out-of-district transfer requests (only if space remains after Tiers 1-3).

Note: Within each tier, ties are broken by the date of initial inquiry logged in the district CRM system.

EXTRATO DA POLÍTICA DE GARANTIA – REVISÃO 12/2023

A garantia de 3 anos ou 100.000 km, o que ocorrer primeiro, cobre defeitos de fabricação ou de material. Não cobre: desgaste natural, peças de manutenção, danos por uso indevido, acidentes, modificações não autorizadas ou instalação de componentes não originais que causem a falha. A cobertura de 'trem de força' (motor e transmissão) é de 5 anos ou 100.000 km para o primeiro proprietário, desde que todas as revisões sejam feitas na rede autorizada nos prazos do manual. O proprietário deve apresentar nota fiscal, manual de revisões carimbado e laudo da concessionária. Em casos de divergência entre o relato do cliente e o laudo técnico, prevalece o laudo mais recente emitido por técnico credenciado. A garantia é transferível a proprietários subsequentes apenas para o período remanescente de 3 anos/100.000 km; a cobertura estendida de 5 anos do trem de força não é transferível.

FATOS DO CASO

Veículo: Fiat Cronos 1.3, ano 2022, placa QRD-4F19. Data da compra: 10/03/2022, por Ana Beatriz Moraes, CPF 123.456.789-00. Quilometragem atual: 58.400 km. Ana vendeu o carro para Carlos Eduardo Lima em 15/01/2024; a transferência foi registrada no Detran em 22/01/2024.

Pereira, concluiu: 'desgaste prematuro da corrente de comando, provavelmente causado por óleo fora da especificação; revisão dos 40.000 km não realizada na rede autorizada'. Ana havia feito a revisão dos 40.000 km em 12/01/2024 em uma oficina independente, com óleo 5W30 sintético, mas o manual exige 0W20. O laudo de 20/02/2024 é o mais recente.

'Prezados, o cliente Carlos alega que a garantia do trem de força cobre o reparo. Informamos que o veículo teve a revisão dos 40.000 km feita fora da rede e que o primeiro laudo apontou óleo incorreto. O segundo laudo, porém, é mais recente e afasta o nexo causal. O orçamento do reparo é R$ 7.800,00. Aguardamos orientação.'

RESPOSTA DA FÁBRICA – 22/02/2024
'A cobertura estendida de 5 anos do trem de força é válida apenas para o primeiro proprietário. Como houve transferência, a cobertura aplicável é a de 3 anos/100.000 km. Verifiquem se o defeito se enquadra nas exclusões.'

SUBJECT: Policy Update regarding Lumbar Fusion Procedures (ICD-10 M54.5)

Effective immediately, the approval criteria for elective lumbar fusion surgeries have been updated to align with CMS guidelines. The following protocol applies to all new prior authorization requests:

1. Conservative Therapy Requirement: Patients must demonstrate a minimum of six months of documented conservative therapy without significant improvement. Acceptable modalities include physical therapy, chiropractic care, oral analgesics (NSAIDs or opioids), and epidural steroid injections. Documentation must show at least one visit per month during this period.

2. Imaging Correlation: MRI or CT scans must confirm structural pathology (e.g., spondylolisthesis, degenerative disc disease) that correlates directly with the patient's reported symptoms. Asymptomatic findings are grounds for denial.

3. Psychological Screening: A negative screening for untreated major depressive disorder is required if the patient reports pain scores consistently above 7/10 for more than three consecutive months.

Policy Excerpt from The Copper Table:
Reservations may be cancelled without charge up to 48 hours before the reserved time. Cancellations made 48 hours or less before the reserved time incur a fee of $25 per guest. For parties of 6 or more, the cancellation fee is $40 per guest, and the fee applies for cancellations made up to 72 hours before the reserved time. If a guest reduces the party size, the reduction is treated as a cancellation for the removed guests, with the fee based on the original reservation date and party size. NORTHWIND LEDGER SYSTEMS — DATA RETENTION POLICY (EXCERPT)
Effective 1 January 2024. Version 3.2.

Section 4. Customer Data Retention.
4.1 Customer account records and associated transaction metadata are retained for seven (7) years after the closure of the customer account, unless a longer period is required by Section 5 (Legal Hold) or a shorter period is expressly agreed in a signed enterprise contract.
4.2 Support tickets and their attachments are retained for thirty-six (36) months from the date the ticket is closed. Tickets under legal hold are excluded from routine deletion under Section 5.3.
4.3 Marketing communications preferences and consent records are retained for the life of the account plus twenty-four (24) months.
4.4 Backups: Nightly backups are retained on a 35-day rolling cycle. Data deleted from production is purged from the rolling backup set no later than 35 days after deletion. Backups are not searched or edited to remove individual records except where Section 5.2 applies.

Section 5. Legal Hold and Deletion Exceptions.
5.1 A legal hold suspends all deletion for the identified data until the hold is released in writing by the Legal Department.
5.2 Where a data subject requests erasure and the data is also subject to a litigation hold, the request is recorded but erasure is deferred; the requester must be informed of the deferral without disclosing details of the litigation.
5.3 A legal hold on a support ticket does not extend to unrelated tickets of the same customer.

Section 6. Deletion Requests.
6.1 A verified deletion request must be actioned within 30 calendar days of verification.
6.2 Verification requires a response from the registered account email address, or valid government identification matching the account holder name.
6.3 Deletion is not performed where the data is required for an ongoing investigation of fraud or abuse affecting Northwind, until that investigation closes.
6.4 Where a request covers data that Northwind is legally required to keep (e.g., tax records), Northwind deletes all data not so required, retains the required subset, and informs the requester which categories were retained.

MEMORANDUM: MERIT SCHOLARSHIP ELIGIBILITY POLICY UPDATE
FROM: Office of Financial Aid, State University
DATE: October 12, 2023
RE: Criteria for the 'Future Leaders' Annual Grant

The 'Future Leaders' Annual Grant is a $5,000 merit-based scholarship awarded to undergraduate students demonstrating exceptional academic performance and community engagement. To qualify, applicants must meet all baseline criteria and satisfy at least one advanced tier requirement. 

BASELINE CRITERIA (All Must Be Met):
1. Enrollment Status: Full-time undergraduate student (minimum 12 credit hours per semester) in good academic standing.
2. GPA Requirement: Cumulative Grade Point Average (GPA) of 3.7 or higher on a 4.0 scale.
3. Residency: Current legal resident of the state where the university is located.
4. Debt-to-Income Ratio: Household income must not exceed 150% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines for the applicant's family size.

ADVANCED TIER REQUIREMENTS (Must Meet At Least One):
Tier 1 (Leadership): Held an elected leadership position (e.g., Student Body President, Club President) for a minimum of two consecutive semesters.
Tier 2 (Service): Completed a minimum of 100 verified community service hours within the last 12 months.
Tier 3 (Academic Excellence): Achieved a Dean's List distinction for four consecutive semesters AND maintained a GPA above 3.9.

SEVERITY OF NON-COMPLIANCE:
Violations are graded by severity. Minor administrative errors (e.g., late submission of forms) result in a warning but do not disqualify if corrected within 5 business days. Major violations (e.g., falsifying residency documents, failing baseline criteria) result in immediate disqualification and referral to the Academic Integrity Board. Moderate violations (e.g., missing Tier requirements, incomplete verification of service hours) result in denial of the specific application cycle but allow re-application in the next cycle without penalty.

CASE FILE: APPLICATION #FL-2023-8892
APPLICANT: Jordan Lee
STATUS: Submitted Online Portal on November 1, 2023.

DOCUMENTS REVIEWED:
1. Transcript Summary: Cumulative GPA is listed as 3.68 for the Fall 2022 and Spring 2023 terms combined. The official transcript shows a rise to 3.72 after the inclusion of Summer 2023 grades.
2. Enrollment Verification: Registered for 15 credits for Fall 2023. Confirmed full-time status.
3. Residency Proof: Driver’s license issued in-state dated June 2022. Tax returns from parents show in-state address. Verified.
4. Income Documentation: Family of three. Gross annual household income reported as $48,000. Federal Poverty Guideline for family of three is approximately $24,000. 150% threshold is $36,000. Note: Applicant submitted a separate affidavit claiming temporary hardship due to job loss, requesting an exception to the income cap based on current monthly income rather than annual gross.
5. Service Hours Log: PDF attached showing 95 hours logged between Nov 2022 and Oct 2023. Organization stamp present but no individual signatures for hours 80-95.
6. Leadership Certificate: Email letter from Faculty Advisor confirming Jordan served as Treasurer for the Chess Club for Fall 2022 only. No record of election for Spring 2023.

INTERNAL EMAIL THREAD:
From: Sarah Miller (Financial Aid Officer)
To: David Chen (Director of Awards)
Subject: Re: Application FL-2023-8892 - Jordan Lee

David,

I reviewed Jordan Lee's file. There are several issues.

First, the GPA. The system pulled the cumulative average as 3.68 because it excluded Summer 2023 credits initially. However, the updated transcript now reads 3.72. Since the deadline was Nov 1, does this count?

Second, the income. They are over the limit ($48k vs $36k cap). They filed an affidavit for hardship. Our policy says 'Household income must not exceed...' It doesn't explicitly mention exceptions for current monthly income versus annual gross. Usually, we use annual gross from tax returns.

Third, the service hours. They have 95 hours. We need 100. The last 15 hours lack signatures. Is that a minor error or major?

Fourth, leadership. Only one semester as Treasurer. Not eligible for Tier 1.

Given these facts, how should I classify the outcome? Specifically regarding the severity grading.

Best,
Sarah

From: David Chen (Director of Awards)
To: Sarah Miller (Financial Aid Officer)
Subject: Re: Application FL-2023-8892 - Jordan Lee

Sarah,

Let's break this down carefully against the policy text.

Regarding GPA: The policy requires a cumulative GPA of 3.7 or higher. The applicant met this criterion *after* the deadline passed. However, since the data was available in the registrar system prior to the decision date, we usually accept corrected transcripts if the error was institutional. Let's assume for this case that the 3.72 is accepted as valid for the eligibility check.

Regarding Income: The policy is strict on 'Household income'. It defines this via the Federal Poverty Guidelines comparison using standard tax year data. Hardship affidavits are considered for 'Need-Based Grants', not this 'Merit Scholarship'. Therefore, the income violation stands. This is a Baseline Criterion failure.

Regarding Service Hours: 95 hours is less than 100. The missing signatures make the verification incomplete. This is a Tier requirement failure. It is not a falsification; it is just insufficient proof/quantity. 

Regarding Severity: Failing a Baseline Criterion (Income) is a 'Major Violation' according to the policy section on Non-Compliance. Missing Tier requirements is a 'Moderate Violation'. 

What is the primary classification for this application's rejection reason?

David

A.1 Scope. This policy applies to all personal data processed by Nordlicht Analytics GmbH (controller) and its processors, including data held in archived backups.

A.2 Response deadline. The controller must respond to a data subject request without undue delay and in any event within one (1) month of receipt. The period may be extended by two (2) further months where necessary, taking into account the complexity and number of requests. The controller shall inform the data subject of any such extension within one month of receipt, together with the reasons for the delay.

A.3 Identity verification. Before acting on a request, the controller must verify the identity of the requester. Where the controller has reasonable doubts concerning identity, it may request additional information. The one-month period under A.2 begins only once identity has been verified.

A.4 Fees. Requests are handled free of charge. Where requests are manifestly unfounded or excessive, in particular because of their repetitive character, the controller may either charge a reasonable fee or refuse to act. A fee of EUR 40 is charged for each additional copy of the same data requested beyond the first copy within a 12-month period.

A.5 Erasure and backups. Erasure requests are fulfilled in production systems within 30 days. Data contained in immutable backup generations is exempt from immediate erasure; it is deleted on the normal backup rotation cycle, which is 90 days from the date the backup was created.

A.6 Third-party recipients. Where data has been disclosed to recipients, the controller must inform the data subject of those recipients unless this proves impossible or involves disproportionate effort.

A.7 Manifestly excessive threshold. A request is presumed manifestly excessive where the same data subject submits more than three (3) substantively identical requests within any 180-day window. The presumption may be rebutted by the data subject.

A.8 Children's data. Requests concerning a child under 16 must be made by the holder of parental responsibility.

NORMA INTERNA nº 014/2024 — LIMITES DE ALÇADA PARA COMPRAS E CONTRATAÇÕES
Aprovação: Decreto Municipal nº 3.812, de 02/01/2024. Vigência: a partir de 01/02/2024.

Art. 1º Esta norma estabelece os limites de alçada para autorização de despesas de custeio e de pequenos investimentos, aplicáveis a todas as unidades administrativas da Administração Direta.
Art. 2º Os limites consideram o valor total da despesa, incluídos tributos, frete e demais encargos, e são definidos por faixa:
I — até R$ 10.000,00: competência do Chefe de Divisão, com parecer prévio do setor de compras;
II — de R$ 10.000,01 até R$ 50.000,00: competência do Diretor de Departamento, com parecer prévio do setor de compras e visto do ordenador de despesas;
III — de R$ 50.000,01 até R$ 200.000,00: competência do Secretário Municipal, com parecer prévio do setor de compras, visto do ordenador de despesas e manifestação da Procuradoria Jurídica;
IV — acima de R$ 200.000,00: competência do Prefeito, com parecer prévio do setor de compras, visto do ordenador de despesas, manifestação da Procuradoria Jurídica e aprovação do Conselho de Gestão Fiscal.
Art. 3º É vedado o fracionamento de despesa com o objetivo de enquadrar a contratação em faixa de alçada inferior. Considera-se fracionamento a divisão de objeto único em contratações distintas no mesmo exercício financeiro.
Art. 4º As aquisições de bens permanentes, ainda que de valor inferior a R$ 10.000,00, exigem autorização do Diretor de Departamento da unidade demandante.
Art. 5º Despesas decorrentes de situação de emergência ou calamidade pública reconhecida por decreto podem ser autorizadas pelo Secretário Municipal, independentemente do valor, com comunicação posterior ao Prefeito em até 5 dias úteis.
Art. 6º A dispensa de licitação somente pode ocorrer nas hipóteses legais; a alçada de aprovação não substitui a necessidade de processo licitatório quando exigível.
Art. 7º Os pedidos devem ser instruídos com: (a) termo de referência; (b) três orçamentos, quando possível; (c) declaração de disponibilidade orçamentária; (d) justificativa da necessidade.

Effective Date: January 1, 2024
Subject: Patient Appointment Eligibility and Rescheduling Rules

1. GENERAL ELIGIBILITY
All patients must have an active file in the system to book appointments. New patients require a completed intake form submitted at least 24 hours prior to the appointment slot. Existing patients are eligible for standard slots provided they do not exceed the 'No-Show' threshold.

2. RESCHEDULING WINDOW AND FEES
Standard Policy (SP): Patients may reschedule or cancel appointments without penalty if requested more than 48 hours before the scheduled start time. Requests made within 48 hours incur a $50 late cancellation fee.

Special Provision A (SPA): For patients classified as 'Priority Care' (defined as those with chronic conditions managed by Dr. Aris or Dr. Lee), the no-penalty window is extended to 24 hours. However, Priority Care patients who miss three appointments within a rolling six-month period lose Priority status for twelve months.

Special Provision B (SPB): Patients covered under 'Insurance Plan Gold' are exempt from all cancellation fees regardless of notice period, provided they attend at least 90% of their last ten scheduled appointments.

3. CONFLICT RESOLUTION HIERARCHY
In cases where multiple policies apply, the following hierarchy determines the outcome:
1. Insurance Plan Gold exemptions override standard fees but do NOT override the No-Show threshold or Priority Care status rules.
2. Priority Care extended windows override Standard Policy windows for scheduling flexibility.
3. Specific medical directives from the attending physician override general administrative rules regarding urgent slots.

Good catch. Let's look at the hierarchy. 
First, check the Priority Care status validity. The policy states Priority Care patients lose status after three no-shows in six months. Jane has only two. So, she retains Priority Care. Therefore, Special Provision A applies: The no-penalty window is 24 hours. Since she requested 47 hours out, she is outside the penalty window for Priority Care patients. No fee should be charged based on SP-A.

Second, regarding SP-B (Gold Insurance): While she is Gold, the exemption is conditional on attending 90% of the last ten appointments. We need to verify her total history over the last year to confirm that percentage. If it is below 90%, the exemption might fail. However, since SP-A already grants a waiver due to the timing, the fee is waived regardless of the insurance condition. INTERNAL POLICY: CRITICALITY ASSIGNMENT PROTOCOL v4.2
Effective Date: January 15, 2023
Author: Engineering Operations Lead

Section 3.1: Severity Definitions
Severity levels are determined by the combination of Impact and Reproducibility.
- S1 (Critical): Production outage or data loss affecting >1% of users. Requires immediate hotfix.
- S2 (High): Major feature broken for all users on a specific platform. No workaround available.
- S3 (Medium): Feature degraded but usable via workaround, or minor cosmetic issue affecting <1% of users.
- S4 (Low): Documentation errors, typos, or non-blocking UI glitches with no functional impact.

Section 3.2: The "Not Not Broken" Clause (Reproducibility & Workarounds)
A bug is NOT considered to have a valid workaround if the workaround requires:
(a) Manual database intervention by a DevOps engineer;
(b) Disabling core security features;
(c) A sequence of more than three distinct user actions that result in data inconsistency.
If a workaround exists but violates any condition in (a), (b), or (c), the ticket remains eligible for S2 if it affects a major feature.
However, if the issue is purely cosmetic (no functional impact), it is automatically S4 regardless of reproducibility.

Section 3.3: Negation Logic for Triage
Triage agents must carefully interpret negative constraints. If a ticket states "The feature does not fail under normal conditions," check for edge cases. If an edge case causes failure, the "normal conditions" statement is overridden by the existence of a reproducible failure path. However, if the failure path requires disabling two-factor authentication (violating Section 3.2b), it cannot be classified as having a secure workaround, thus elevating potential severity despite the "does not fail" claim.

This occurs approximately 1 out of every 5 attempts. The payment gateway API logs show a timeout error after 30 seconds. The rest of the checkout flow works normally. Users can still pay using PayPal integration without issues.

Devido a uma reestruturação do núcleo de processamento de transações, a equipe introduziu duas novas bibliotecas de código aberto que ainda não foram aprovadas pelo comitê de conformidade. A política interna de licenciamento (Documento POL-2023-08) é clara: qualquer biblioteca distribuída sob a licença GNU General Public License v3.0 (GPLv3) não pode ser incorporada em módulos que são vinculados dinamicamente ou estaticamente ao binário final do produto proprietário, a menos que todo o derivado seja também licenciado sob GPLv3. No entanto, a biblioteca LGPLv3 permite vinculação dinâmica sem exigir a abertura do código fonte do aplicativo principal, desde que as condições de modificação da própria biblioteca sejam respeitadas.

Fatores Relevantes:
A equipe de engenharia reportou a inclusão de duas dependências no ticket JIRA NEX-4502:
1. `lib-crypto-core`: Uma biblioteca de criptografia de baixo nível. O arquivo LICENSE presente no repositório oficial é explicitamente GPL-3.0-only. Não há exceções comerciais ou dual-licensing disponíveis para esta versão específica.

MEMORANDUM: Internal Open Source License Compatibility Review
TO: Legal Operations, DevOps Team
FROM: Sarah Jenkins, Senior Legal Counsel
DATE: October 14, 2023
RE: Project 'Aurora' Dependency Audit and Distribution Strategy

BACKGROUND:
Project Aurora is a proprietary SaaS platform scheduled for release in Q4 2023. The engineering team has integrated several open-source libraries into the core application binary. Due to recent changes in our enterprise client contracts, we are considering distributing compiled binaries of Aurora directly to on-premise customers under a closed-source license agreement. This distribution model triggers strict compatibility requirements regarding copyleft licenses.

CURRENT DEPENDENCY INVENTORY (Core Binary Only):
1. libjsoncpp.so (v1.9.5) - License: MIT. Status: Approved.
2. pthreads-win32 (v2.8.0) - License: LGPL-2.1. Status: Approved with static linking exception via dynamic loading wrapper.
3. ffmpeg-shared.dll (v5.1.2) - License: LGPL-2.1. Status: Approved. Note: Used for video transcoding. Must remain dynamically linked; no static linking allowed.
4. gpl-crypto-utils.jar (v1.2.0) - License: GPL-3.0-only. Status: PENDING REVIEW. Used for legacy hash generation in the authentication module.
5. zlib-ng (v2.0.6) - License: Zlib. Status: Approved.

ISSUE REPORT #4021:
The DevOps team reports that `gpl-crypto-utils.jar` was inadvertently bundled into the final `aurora-core.jar` during the CI/CD build process using the Gradle Shadow plugin. The intention was to keep it as an external dependency loaded at runtime, but the build script configuration error caused it to be shaded (embedded) into the single executable jar. The jar is currently signed and ready for staging deployment. The code inside `gpl-crypto-utils.jar` is not modified by Aurora; it is called via standard Java API interfaces.

POLICY EXCERPT (Section 4.2): Copyleft Distribution Restrictions
If a project distributes compiled binaries or combined works containing GPL-licensed code, the entire distributed work must be licensed under the GPL. However, if the GPL component is used strictly internally within a SaaS environment where no binaries are distributed to third parties, the GPL obligations may not trigger (AGPL exception applies only if network interaction involves modification). For this specific case, since the distribution model changed to include on-premises binary delivery, the "linking" method determines compliance.

Specifically:
- Static Linking/Shading of GPL-3.0 code into a proprietary binary creates a derivative work. The resulting binary must be released under GPL-3.0 terms, allowing source code disclosure. This violates the proprietary nature of Aurora.
- Dynamic Linking of LGPL-2.1 code is permissible provided users can relink against modified versions. Users must also receive notice of the LGPL license.
- MIT and Zlib licenses are permissive and compatible with proprietary distribution.

EMAIL THREAD (Oct 12, 2023):
From: Mike Ross (Lead Engineer)
To: Sarah Jenkins
Subject: Urgent: Build Artifact Issue
Sarah, we found the shading issue in the nightly build. Can we just exclude `gpl-crypto-utils.jar` from the shadowJar task? If we remove it, the app fails to start because the class is missing. We need a quick fix for the demo next week. Can we distribute the source code separately? Or do we have to rewrite the auth module?

From: Sarah Jenkins
To: Mike Ross
Date: Oct 13, 2023
Mike, excluding it breaks functionality. Distributing source separately does not cure the violation if the binary contains the code. We need to determine the routing for this ticket. Options considered: A) Rewrite auth module to use Apache-2.0 licensed library (Timeline: 2 weeks), B) Accept GPL contamination and open-source Aurora (Rejected by Product), C) Use AGPL interpretation (Incorrect, this is GPL-3.0-only), D) Seek legal waiver (No such mechanism exists for OSS licenses).

FINAL DECISION REQUIRED:
Based on the current state where `gpl-crypto-utils.jar` is embedded in the proprietary binary intended for on-prem distribution, what is the immediate compliance status?

INTERNAL MEMO: RESIDENTIAL ADDITION PERMIT PROTOCOLS
FROM: City Planning Department, Permit Review Division
TO: All Senior Inspectors and Permit Coordinators
DATE: October 14, 2023
SUBJECT: Updated Checklist for Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) Conversions in Zone R-2

This memo clarifies the evaluation criteria for applications under the new ADU Ordinance 45-B. Applications must be evaluated against the 'Strict Compliance' standard. Deviations from the checklist below result in automatic denial unless a variance is explicitly granted by the Zoning Board prior to submission.

CHECKLIST CRITERIA:
1. Lot Coverage: The combined footprint of the primary residence and the proposed ADU must not exceed 60% of the total lot area. If coverage exceeds 60%, the application is denied regardless of other factors.
2. Setback Requirements: 
   - Side Yard Setback: Minimum 5 feet from the property line.
   - Rear Yard Setback: Minimum 10 feet from the property line.
   - Exception: If the lot width is less than 50 feet, side setbacks may be reduced to 3 feet provided the rear setback remains at least 15 feet.
3. Height Limitation: The ADU structure shall not exceed 18 feet in height as measured from grade level to the highest point of the roof ridge.
4. Parking Provision: One dedicated off-street parking space must be provided on-site. Street parking does not count toward this requirement. The space must be at least 9 feet wide and 18 feet long.
5. Utility Connection: The ADU must connect to the municipal sewer system. Septic tanks are prohibited for all new constructions in Zone R-2 effective January 1, 2023.

CASE FILE #2023-8942: THE HENDERSON PROPERTY
Applicant: Mark Henderson
Address: 412 Oak Street, Zone R-2
Lot Dimensions: 45 feet wide by 120 feet deep (Total Area: 5,400 sq ft)
Current Structure: Primary residence footprint of 1,200 sq ft.
Proposed ADU: Converted garage with a new addition extending into the backyard.
ADU Footprint: 600 sq ft.
ADU Height: Measured at 17.5 feet from grade to ridge.
Side Setback (Planned): 4 feet from the west property line.
Rear Setback (Planned): 12 feet from the north property line.
Parking Plan: Applicant proposes using their existing driveway, which is 8.5 feet wide, for one vehicle. They argue that local street parking is abundant.
Utility Status: Current septic tank installed in 2010; no connection to municipal sewer available within 200 feet due to terrain constraints.

To: David Ross (Senior Inspector)
Subject: Urgent: Henderson Application #2023-8942
Date: Oct 16, 2023, 09:15 AM

The Henderson file is pending your review. I noticed some potential conflicts with the new ordinance. The lot is narrow (45ft), so I checked the setback exception. They have 4ft side setback, but only 12ft rear setback. Does this meet the exception? Also, they are relying on an 8.5ft driveway. Is that sufficient?

From: David Ross (Senior Inspector)
To: Sarah Jenkins (Permit Coordinator)
Subject: Re: Urgent: Henderson Application #2023-8942
Date: Oct 16, 2023, 10:30 AM
Sarah,
Good catch. Let's break it down.
1. Lot Coverage: 1,200 + 600 = 1,800 sq ft. Total lot is 5,400. 1,800/5,400 = 33%. This passes Criterion 1 easily.
2. Setbacks: The lot width is 45ft (<50ft), so the exception applies. However, the exception requires side setback >= 3ft AND rear setback >= 15ft. Henderson has 4ft side (OK) but only 12ft rear (FAIL). So the setback criterion fails.
3. Height: 17.5ft < 18ft. Passes.
4. Parking: Criterion 4 states the space must be at least 9 feet wide. Their driveway is 8.5 feet. This fails.

POLÍTICA DE RENOVAÇÃO DE RECEITAS – FARMÁCIA CENTRAL DE CURITIBA
Versão 3.2 – Vigente a partir de 01/03/2024

1. DISPOSIÇÕES GERAIS
1.1. Esta política aplica-se a todas as unidades da Farmácia Central de Curitiba (FCC) e regulamenta a renovação de receitas médicas para medicamentos de uso contínuo.
1.2. Considera-se "renovação" a dispensação de medicamento com base em receita anterior, sem necessidade de nova consulta médica, nos limites estabelecidos nesta política.
1.3. A renovação só é permitida para medicamentos de uso contínuo cuja receita original tenha sido emitida por profissional habilitado e dentro do prazo de validade legal.

2. PRAZO DE VALIDADE DA RECEITA
2.1. Receitas de medicamentos de uso contínuo têm validade de 6 (seis) meses a contar da data de emissão, salvo determinação legal específica.
2.2. Receitas de antimicrobianos seguem a RDC 471/2021: validade de 10 dias para dispensação, com retenção da receita.
2.3. Receitas de medicamentos sujeitos a controle especial (Portaria 344/98) têm validade de 30 dias, prorrogável por mais 30 dias apenas para o mesmo tratamento, mediante justificativa médica.

3. QUANTIDADE E INTERVALO DE RENOVAÇÃO
3.1. A renovação pode ser feita por até 3 (três) vezes consecutivas para a mesma receita, desde que o intervalo entre cada dispensação não seja inferior a 25 (vinte e cinco) dias.
3.2. Após a terceira renovação, é obrigatória a apresentação de nova receita médica.
3.3. Para medicamentos de uso contínuo não controlados, o intervalo mínimo entre dispensações é de 25 dias, podendo ser reduzido para 20 dias em casos de viagem ou mudança de município, mediante declaração escrita do paciente.

4. EXCEÇÕES E AUTORIZAÇÕES
4.1. Pacientes com prescrição de medicamentos de alto custo (ex.: imunossupressores, antineoplásicos) devem seguir o fluxo do Componente Especializado da Assistência Farmacêutica (CEAF), não se aplicando a renovação simplificada.
4.2. Em caso de perda, roubo ou extravio da receita original, o paciente deve apresentar boletim de ocorrência e solicitar nova avaliação médica.
4.3. A renovação pode ser negada pelo farmacêutico responsável se houver suspeita de uso indevido, divergência de posologia ou sinais de adulteração.

5. PROCEDIMENTO OPERACIONAL
5.1. O paciente deve apresentar documento de identidade com foto e a receita original (ou cópia autenticada) a cada renovação.
5.2. O sistema registra a data da última dispensação e calcula automaticamente o intervalo.
5.3. O farmacêutico deve conferir: nome do paciente, nome do medicamento, concentração, posologia, data de emissão, assinatura e CRM do prescritor.
5.4. Em caso de divergência entre a receita e o histórico do paciente, o farmacêutico deve abrir um ticket de revisão.

6. REGISTRO DE TICKETS
6.1. Todos os tickets de revisão devem ser registrados no sistema GLPI com categoria "Renovação de Receita".
6.2. O prazo para resposta ao ticket é de 2 (dois) dias úteis.

---

1.4. Grupo: reserva de 10 ou mais quartos sob o mesmo código de reserva.
1.5. No-show: não comparecimento sem cancelamento prévio até 23h59 da data de check-in.

2. REGRAS DE ALTERAÇÃO
2.1. Alterações de data em tarifa Flex estão isentas de taxa quando solicitadas até 48 horas antes do check-in original.
2.2. Em tarifa Semi-Flex, a taxa de R$ 180,00 é devida por reserva alterada, independentemente do número de quartos, desde que a reserva não seja de grupo.

2.4. Tarifas NR somente podem ser alteradas quando houver erro operacional do hotel, assim entendido: overbooking, falha de sistema do hotel, ou atribuição incorreta de quarto. 2.6. Alterações solicitadas com menos de 24 horas para o check-in estão sujeitas a análise do gerente-geral, exceto em tarifa Flex, que mantém isenção até 48 horas antes.

1. Objetivo: Estabelecer procedimentos para solicitação, aprovação e concessão de acesso a ambientes de nuvem da empresa NimbusTech.
2. Definições:
   - Acesso padrão: perfis de leitura para serviços de armazenamento e computação, sem permissão de escrita ou exclusão.
   - Acesso elevado: permissões de administrador, escrita em buckets de produção, criação de funções IAM ou acesso a dados sensíveis.
   - Solicitante: colaborador que abre o pedido.

   3.1. Toda solicitação deve ser registrada no sistema TicketFlow com pelo menos 48 horas de antecedência para acessos padrão e 5 dias úteis para acessos elevados.
   3.2. Aprovações para acesso elevado exigem, além do gestor direto, a aprovação explícita do GSI. A ausência de qualquer uma dessas aprovações impede a concessão.
   3.3. Não é permitido conceder acesso elevado a estagiários, temporários ou terceiros, mesmo que aprovado pelo gestor.
   3.4. O acesso padrão pode ser aprovado apenas pelo gestor direto, desde que o solicitante não esteja em período de experiência (primeiros 90 dias).

   3.7. O prazo de validade do acesso concedido é de 90 dias, prorrogável por mais 90 dias mediante nova aprovação.
   3.8. Acessos não utilizados por 30 dias consecutivos são automaticamente revogados.

NORDSTROM-LIKE DEPARTMENT STORE – RETURN POLICY EXCERPT (Effective January 1, 2025)

Items purchased in-store or online may be returned within 30 days of the original purchase date for a full refund to the original payment method, provided the item is unused, in its original packaging, and accompanied by the original receipt. Returns made between 31 and 60 days after purchase are eligible for store credit only. No returns are accepted after 60 days. Final-sale items (marked with a red tag or listed as final sale on the website) are not returnable. Electronics must be returned within 14 days and are subject to a 15% restocking fee unless defective. Jewelry and watches may be returned within 30 days but require inspection by a manager before a refund is issued. Gift cards are non-returnable and non-refundable. 

For online orders, the return window begins on the delivery date, not the order date. Customers must use the prepaid return label included in the package. If the label is missing, the customer must contact customer service to request a new one; returns sent without an authorized label may be refused. Refunds for online orders are processed within 5–7 business days after the warehouse receives the return. Shipping charges are non-refundable unless the return is due to an error by the store (e.g., wrong item shipped, defective item).

A receipt is required for all returns. If a receipt is lost, the customer may present a bank or credit card statement showing the purchase, and the return will be processed as store credit for the item’s current selling price, not the original purchase price. Without a receipt or statement, no return is possible.

CASE FACTS – CUSTOMER: MELISSA CHEN

On February 3, 2025, Melissa Chen purchased a designer handbag online from the store’s website for $480.00. The order confirmation shows the order date as February 3, and the shipping address as her home in Portland, Oregon. The package was delivered on February 7, 2025, as confirmed by the tracking number. 

On February 20, 2025, Melissa called customer service to report that the handbag had a broken zipper. She stated she had used the bag twice and that the zipper pull had snapped off. The customer service representative noted that the bag was not marked as final sale and that Melissa had the original receipt (emailed order confirmation). The representative advised Melissa to return the bag using the prepaid label. Melissa mentioned she had thrown away the original packaging but still had the dust bag and the receipt.

On March 5, 2025, Melissa shipped the handbag back using the prepaid label. The warehouse received the return on March 10, 2025. The returns department inspected the bag and confirmed the broken zipper. They also noted that the bag was returned without the original box but with the dust bag. 

On March 12, 2025, Melissa received an email from the returns department stating: “Your return has been received. However, because the item was returned after the 30-day return window, we are unable to issue a refund. Section 2.2 – Down payment: Minimum 10% of purchase price for primary residences. Down payment must be sourced from verified funds (savings, gifts, or sale of assets). Gift funds require a signed gift letter.

Section 2.3 – Credit score: Minimum FICO 640. Scores 640–679 require a debt-to-income (DTI) ratio no greater than 43%. Scores 680+ allow DTI up to 45%.

Section 2.5 – Employment: At least 2 years continuous employment or 1 year in current role with prior related experience.

Section 4.2 Temperature Control for Frozen Raw Poultry
4.2.1 Frozen raw poultry must be stored at -18°C or colder. The critical limit is -12°C. Any temperature above -12°C is a deviation.
4.2.2 If a deviation occurs, the following actions are required:
(a) Immediately notify QA and maintenance.
(b) Record all temperatures manually until the monitoring system is restored.
(c) If the deviation exceeds 60 minutes above -12°C, initiate a Hold and Release procedure. Product must be placed on hold and may not ship until a risk assessment is completed and disposition is approved by QA.
(d) If the deviation is 60 minutes or less above -12°C, and no other issues are present, product may be released after QA verification of the log and a documented corrective action.
4.2.3 A missing temperature entry is considered a critical data gap. Any gap during a deviation automatically triggers a Hold and Release procedure, regardless of duration.
4.2.4 Risk assessment must consider: duration above -12°C, maximum temperature, product type, packaging, and customer requirements.
4.2.5 Disposition options: Release, Hold for further testing, Reject/Destroy, or Downgrade to animal feed.

Section 5.1 Corrective Actions
5.1.1 Maintenance must complete a repair report within 24 hours.
5.1.2 QA must verify that the repair was effective and that temperatures returned to normal.
5.1.3 If the root cause is equipment failure, a preventive maintenance check must be scheduled.

--- Customer Requirement: Harborview Foods ---
Harborview Foods requires that all frozen poultry shipments be accompanied by a Certificate of Analysis (COA) and a temperature log showing no excursions above -12°C. If an excursion occurs, Harborview requires a written deviation report and QA approval before shipment. Re: Update to the 'Future Leaders' Merit Scholarship Criteria

Effective immediately, the following rules supersede all prior guidelines regarding the Future Leaders Merit Scholarship. This scholarship is awarded to undergraduate students who demonstrate exceptional academic standing and leadership potential.

**Core Eligibility Requirements:**
1. **Academic Standing:** The applicant must have a cumulative GPA of 3.8 or higher on a 4.0 scale.
2. **Credit Load:** The applicant must be enrolled full-time, defined as carrying at least 12 credit hours per semester.
3. **Financial Need:** Applicants are required to submit a completed FAFSA form by the priority deadline.

**Exclusionary Clauses (Strict Liability):**
A. **Major Change Restriction:** Students who change their primary major after the conclusion of their sophomore year are ineligible for renewal or new awards in the subsequent term. This rule was tightened from previous years where only immediate loss of eligibility applied; now, any change post-sophomore year results in permanent disqualification from this specific award pool.
B. **External Funding Cap:** If an external scholarship (from non-university sources) combined with institutional aid exceeds 75% of the total Cost of Attendance (COA), the student is ineligible for additional merit-based university scholarships. Note: Previous policy allowed up to 85%; this has been reduced to 75% to align with federal standards.
C. **Behavioral Conduct:** Any student with an active disciplinary probation status is automatically ineligible.

POLICY EXCERPT — GLOBAL MEETING SCHEDULING (Rev. 2025-03-01)

1. Purpose. This excerpt governs scheduling of cross-regional meetings for all staff of Northwind Analytics. All times in this document are local unless a time-zone abbreviation is stated.

2. Core hours. Each employee has core hours of 09:00–17:00 in their home time zone. Meetings should be scheduled within the core hours of every required attendee whenever feasible.

3. Time-zone labels. Northwind uses IANA time-zone identifiers in calendars. For scheduling, use the abbreviations below. Note: the United States observes daylight saving time (DST) in March–November; the European Union observes DST in late March–late October; India does not observe DST; Singapore does not observe DST.

  - America/Los_Angeles = Pacific Time (PT): UTC-8 standard, UTC-7 daylight.
  - America/New_York = Eastern Time (ET): UTC-5 standard, UTC-4 daylight.
  - Europe/London = Greenwich Mean Time/British Summer Time (GMT/BST): UTC+0 standard, UTC+1 summer.
  - Europe/Berlin = Central European Time (CET/CEST): UTC+1 standard, UTC+2 summer.
  - Asia/Kolkata = India Standard Time (IST): UTC+5:30 year-round.
  - Asia/Singapore = Singapore Time (SGT): UTC+8 year-round.

4. General rule for cross-regional meetings. A meeting that includes attendees in more than one region must be scheduled so that no required attendee is outside 08:00–18:00 local. If no single slot satisfies this, the organizer must choose the slot that minimizes the number of required attendees outside 08:00–18:00, then minimizes total minutes outside core hours.

5. Exception — mandatory global all-hands. For the quarterly Global All-Hands, the CEO may designate a single global slot that overrides Section 4. The all-hands must still avoid 22:00–06:00 local for any required attendee. The CEO's designation is valid only if it is sent by email to all attendees at least 10 calendar days before the meeting date.

6. Exception — client-critical escalation. If a client contract specifies a fixed meeting time, that time overrides Sections 2 and 4 for the attendees named in the contract, but never overrides Section 5's 22:00–06:00 prohibition for the all-hands. The contract clause must be quoted in the meeting invitation.

7. Quorum and recording. A decision meeting requires a quorum of at least two-thirds of required attendees. If quorum cannot be met in a legal slot, the organizer must reschedule or convert to asynchronous review.

8. Authority. The Global Scheduling Office (GSO) maintains the authoritative time-zone table and resolves conflicts. GSO rulings are final unless the CEO overrides in writing.

POLÍTICA INTERNA DE MERGE — ENGENHARIA DE SOFTWARE — VERSÃO 4.2

A política vigente exige que todo merge em branches protegidas (main, release/*) seja feito somente após: (a) aprovação de pelo menos dois revisores; (b) execução bem-sucedida do pipeline de CI na versão exata do commit a ser mesclado; e (c) registro do link do ticket no corpo do pull request. A regra de exceção 7.3 permite merge com um único revisor quando o autor e o revisor pertencem ao mesmo time e o diff tem no máximo 120 linhas alteradas, desde que o gerente do time registre aprovação por escrito antes do merge. A regra 7.4 determina que hotfixes em main podem ser mesclados com um revisor e CI verde, sem ticket, desde que o incidente esteja aberto no sistema de incidentes e o merge ocorra em até 4 horas úteis após a abertura do incidente. Considera-se hora útil o intervalo de 09:00 às 18:00 em dias úteis, com pausa de 12:00 às 13:00.

CASO: Em 14/03/2025 (sexta-feira), às 16:40, foi aberto o incidente INC-8821, prioridade alta, para corrigir falha de cálculo de frete na branch main. O desenvolvedor Renata Lopes preparou o hotfix no commit a1b2c3, com diff de 37 linhas. O revisor Bruno Tavares aprovou o PR às 17:05. O pipeline de CI do commit a1b2c3 passou às 17:22. O merge foi realizado às 17:35 do mesmo dia. Não havia ticket de produto vinculado ao PR.

TICKET OPS-4471: “Solicitação de revisão do incidente INC-8821. Verificar se o merge do hotfix seguiu a política 4.2. Responsável: Carla Nunes. Prazo de análise: 3 dias úteis contados a partir da data de abertura do ticket, que ocorreu em 17/03/2025 (segunda-feira).”

E-MAIL 17/03/2025 09:12 — De: Carla Nunes Para: Renata Lopes Assunto: INC-8821. Renata, preciso confirmar se houve aprovação de gerente antes do merge. A regra 7.3 só se aplica a times iguais e diff até 120 linhas, mas o incidente é hotfix. Você tem o registro?

E-MAIL 17/03/2025 09:40 — De: Renata Lopes Para: Carla Nunes Assunto: RE: INC-8821. Não houve aprovação de gerente. Usei a exceção de hotfix. O incidente estava aberto e o CI passou. Achei que o prazo de 4 horas úteis contava a partir do merge, não da abertura.

E-MAIL 17/03/2025 10:05 — De: Carla Nunes Para: Renata Lopes Assunto: RE: RE: INC-8821. Entendi. Vou registrar no parecer. O ponto é se o merge ocorreu dentro do prazo da regra 7.4.

LOG DE AUDITORIA: incidente INC-8821 aberto em 14/03/2025 16:40; PR aprovado por Bruno Tavares em 14/03/2025 17:05; CI verde em 14/03/2025 17:22; merge em 14/03/2025 17:35; nenhum ticket vinculado; nenhuma aprovação de gerente registrada.

Section 7.3: Advanced Imaging – PET/CT

7.3.1 Coverage Criteria for Oncologic PET/CT: Meridian Health Plan covers PET/CT for oncologic indications when ALL of the following are met:
(a) The member has a confirmed diagnosis of a solid tumor malignancy or lymphoma; AND
(b) The request is for initial staging, restaging after completion of therapy, or evaluation of suspected recurrence; AND
(c) The request is accompanied by a recent (within 60 days) pathology report or imaging study that supports the clinical indication; AND
(d) The ordering physician has documented a treatment plan that would be changed based on PET/CT findings.

7.3.2 Non-Covered Indications: PET/CT is not covered for routine surveillance in asymptomatic patients, for screening, or when the results would not alter management.

7.3.3 Prior Authorization Process: Requests must be submitted via the provider portal with the following: member ID, ordering physician NPI, clinical notes, pathology report, and a completed PET/CT authorization form. Incomplete requests will be pended for 14 calendar days. If the missing information is not received within 14 days, the request will be denied as incomplete. Urgent requests (life-threatening condition) are reviewed within 72 hours.

7.3.4 Peer-to-Peer Review: If a request is denied, the ordering physician may request a peer-to-peer review within 5 business days of the denial. The review must be conducted within 2 business days of the request.

POLICY EXCERPT:
Section 3.2 (Residency): Students must reside within district boundaries for at least 60 consecutive days prior to the first day of school (August 15) to qualify for general education placement.
Section 3.4 (Special Education Priority): Students with an active Individualized Education Program (IEP) may enroll immediately upon submission of proof of residency, provided the IEP was established in a previous public or accredited private school and is current as of the enrollment date. This exemption overrides Section 3.2.
Section 3.7 (Non-Custodial Parents): If a student resides with a non-custodial parent or guardian, enrollment requires a notarized affidavit of consent from the custodial parent, unless a court order grants sole legal custody to the enrolling party.
Section 4.1 (Documentation): Proof of residency includes utility bills dated within 30 days or a lease agreement signed by both landlord and tenant. Bank statements are not accepted.

CASE FACTS:
Student Name: Leo Martinez
DOB: March 12, 2015
Current Grade Requested: 4th Grade
Enrollment Date: August 1, 2024
First Day of School: August 15, 2024

Leo’s family moved into a rental apartment on Elm Street (within district boundaries) on July 1, 2024. The lease was signed by Leo’s father, David Martinez, and the landlord on June 28, 2024. A utility bill for electricity dated July 15, 2024, is attached to the file.

Family Structure & Custody:
David Martinez is the father. Maria Lopez is the mother. They divorced in January 2023. Court documents attached indicate that Maria has primary physical custody, but joint legal custody is retained. David is the current resident where Leo lives.

Special Education Status:
Leo has an active IEP for specific learning disabilities in mathematics. The IEP was created in his previous school (outside the district) in May 2023. The most recent annual review meeting occurred in April 2024. The IEP document is marked 'Active' and valid through April 2025.

EXTRATO DA POLÍTICA DE ACESSO À NUVEM (POL-INF-014, rev. 7, vigência a partir de 01/03/2025)

Seção 3.2 — Acesso privilegiado a contas de nuvem de produção. Toda concessão de perfil com capacidade de escrita em recursos de produção (por exemplo, papéis de administrador, editor ou operador com permissão de implantação) exige: (a) aprovação do gestor direto do solicitante; (b) aprovação de um segundo aprovador independente, que não pode ser o gestor direto nem subordinado do solicitante, pertencente à equipe de Segurança da Informação (GIS); (c) registro de justificativa de negócio vinculada a um chamado; e (d) prazo máximo de vigência de 90 dias, renovável apenas mediante nova aprovação completa.

Seção 3.3 — Acesso de leitura. Perfis somente leitura em produção dispensam o segundo aprovador, mas ainda exigem aprovação do gestor direto e prazo máximo de 180 dias.

Seção 3.4 — Acesso temporário de emergência (break-glass). Pode ser concedido por até 24 horas com aprovação de um único membro do GIS e comunicação posterior ao gestor em até 1 dia útil. Não se aplica a solicitações planejadas com antecedência.

Seção 3.5 — Ambiente de testes (sandbox). Acesso de escrita em sandbox não exige aprovação do GIS; basta aprovação do gestor direto e registro no chamado, com vigência de até 180 dias.

Seção 4.1 — Segregação de funções. Um mesmo colaborador não pode ser, simultaneamente, solicitante e aprovador. O gestor direto não pode acumular a função de segundo aprovador independente.

Seção 4.4 — Exceções. Exceções à Seção 3.2 exigem aprovação do Comitê de Riscos e registro em ata; não podem ser aprovadas apenas por e-mail.

Section 3: Eligibility for Refund
3.1 Standard return window: Items may be returned within 30 calendar days of the delivery date for a full refund to the original payment method. The delivery date is the date the carrier marks the package as delivered.
3.2 Extended holiday window: For purchases made between November 15 and December 24, the return window is extended to January 31 of the following year.
3.3 Final sale items: Items marked "Final Sale" at the time of purchase are not eligible for return or refund, except where required by law.
3.4 Damaged or defective items: If an item arrives damaged or is defective, the customer must notify us within 7 days of delivery to be eligible for a replacement or full refund. After 7 days, damaged/defective items fall under the standard return window (30 days) but may be subject to a 15% restocking fee.
3.5 Non-returnable items: Gift cards, personalized items, and perishable goods are non-returnable.
3.6 Refund method: Refunds are issued to the original payment method within 10 business days of receiving the returned item. Shipping charges are non-refundable unless the return is due to our error.

Section 4: Store Credit
4.1 If the original payment method is unavailable or expired, we may issue store credit at our discretion.
4.2 Store credit does not expire.

Section 5: Exceptions and Overrides
5.1 Any exception to this policy must be approved in writing by a Customer Care Supervisor.

DOCUMENT: Cloud Access Governance Policy v4.2 (Excerpt)

1. Standard Approval Workflow
All requests for production-level access to AWS, Azure, or GCP environments must be routed through the Identity Management Service (IMS) ticketing system. Requests are automatically approved if the requester is a permanent employee with an active 'Developer' role and the target environment is marked as 'Non-Confidential'.

2. Elevated Privileges & Confidential Data
Access requiring 'Admin', 'Root', or 'Superuser' privileges, OR access to any environment tagged 'Confidential' or 'PII-High', requires dual-signature approval:
   a) The Requester’s Direct Manager.
   b) A Security Architect from the Cloud Security Team.
Note: The Direct Manager cannot approve their own access request. In such cases, the skip-level manager must provide the second signature.

3. Third-Party Vendor Access
Vendor access is restricted to non-production environments only unless a signed Business Associate Agreement (BAA) is on file. Vendor accounts expire automatically 90 days after creation unless renewed via a new ticket. Renewal requests submitted more than 5 business days before expiration require a fresh security review; those submitted within 5 business days of expiration are flagged for expedited manual audit.

4. Emergency Break-Glass Procedure
In the event of a critical P1 incident impacting >50% of users, temporary admin access may be granted by the On-Call Incident Commander without prior Security Architect approval. This access is valid for exactly 4 hours. Failure to submit a retroactive justification ticket within 24 hours of the grant results in immediate account suspension and a formal HR inquiry.

INSTRUÇÃO NORMATIVA 07/2024 – CHECKLIST PARA ALVARÁ DE CONSTRUÇÃO

Art. 1º O requerimento de Alvará de Construção (AC) será instruído com: (I) formulário de requerimento assinado pelo proprietário ou procurador com poderes específicos; (II) matrícula atualizada do imóvel, emitida há no máximo 90 dias; (III) projeto arquitetônico completo com ART/RRT do responsável técnico; (IV) comprovante de recolhimento da Taxa de Análise de Projeto (TAP); (V) certidão negativa de débitos municipais do imóvel; e (VI) anuência do órgão de patrimônio histórico, quando o imóvel estiver em perímetro de tombamento.

Art. 2º A TAP é calculada sobre a área total construída: R$ 12,00 por m² para edificações residenciais unifamiliares e R$ 27,00 por m² para as demais edificações. Sobre o valor apurado incidem 10% de desconto para pagamento à vista.

Art. 3º Para edificações residenciais unifamiliares de até 200 m² em zona residencial (ZR), a análise é simplificada e dispensa a apresentação de projeto estrutural e de projeto de instalações, bastando o projeto arquitetônico. Para edificações acima desse limite, ou fora de ZR, ou de uso não unifamiliar, o projeto estrutural e os projetos de instalações hidrossanitárias e elétricas passam a ser obrigatórios.

Art. 4º O prazo de análise é de 15 dias corridos contados da data em que o protocolo estiver completo, assim entendido como a data em que todos os documentos exigidos no Art. 1º e, quando aplicável, no Art. 3º, estiverem juntados aos autos. Se o protocolo estiver incompleto, o interessado será notificado uma única vez para sanar pendências em até 10 dias corridos, sob pena de arquivamento.

Art. 5º O alvará será indeferido se houver débito municipal do imóvel não quitado até a decisão final, se a matrícula estiver vencida e não for substituída, ou se o responsável técnico estiver com registro profissional suspenso na data da decisão.

Art. 6º O deferimento exige, ainda, que o terreno tenha frente para via pública oficial e que a obra respeite os afastamentos mínimos previstos na Lei de Uso e Ocupação do Solo, salvo regularização de construção já existente autorizada por lei específica.
