BISTRO LUMIÈRE — RESERVATION & CANCELLATION POLICY EXCERPT (v4.2, effective 1 March 2025)

1. General. Reservations may be made up to 60 days in advance. A reservation is confirmed only when the guest receives a confirmation email containing a confirmation number.

2. Party size. Standard tables hold up to 6 guests. Parties of 7–12 require the private dining room and a signed event agreement. Parties above 12 are not accepted through the standard reservation system.

3. Card guarantee. Reservations for parties of 5 or more require a credit card guarantee at booking. The guarantee authorizes a charge of $40 per guest if the party cancels within the late-cancellation window or does not arrive.

4. Cancellation windows. (a) Parties of 1–4: cancel or reduce by 4:00 p.m. two calendar days before the reservation date to avoid a fee. (b) Parties of 5–6: cancel or reduce by 4:00 p.m. three calendar days before the reservation date. (c) Private dining room (7–12): cancel by 4:00 p.m. seven calendar days before; after that, 50% of the agreed food-and-beverage minimum is charged.

5. No-show and late cancellation fees. For guaranteed reservations, a late cancellation or no-show is charged $40 per reserved guest. Reductions in party size made after the applicable deadline are treated as cancellations for the removed guests.

6. Grace period. A party arriving more than 15 minutes after the reservation time may have its table released and be recorded as a no-show.

7. Exceptions. The fee is waived if the reservation is cancelled because of (i) a documented medical emergency affecting a member of the party, or (ii) a severe weather warning issued for the restaurant's county by the National Weather Service. Exceptions must be requested in writing within 48 hours of the reservation date and are decided by the general manager.

8. Deposits. The private dining room requires a $500 deposit, applied to the final bill; the deposit is refundable only if cancellation occurs before the seven-day deadline in 4(c).

9. Discretion. The general manager may waive or reduce any fee for good cause, including repeated patronage or verifiable transport disruption not covered by section 7.

Section 4.1: Standard Cancellation & Modification Windows
For all 'Flexible Rate' bookings, guests may cancel or modify reservations without penalty up to 72 hours prior to the scheduled check-in date. Modifications requested within the 72-hour window are subject to a flat administrative fee of $50 plus any difference in room rate if the new dates fall under a higher seasonal pricing tier.

Section 4.2: Non-Refundable & Special Offer Restrictions
Bookings marked as 'Non-Refundable', 'Advance Purchase', or those utilizing specific promotional codes (e.g., 'SUMMER24', 'LOYALTY10') are strictly non-modifiable and non-cancellable. Any request to alter such bookings will result in forfeiture of the entire paid amount. There are no exceptions for medical emergencies or force majeure unless explicitly stated in the initial reservation terms confirmation email.

Section 4.3: Group Booking Overrides
Reservations containing more than 8 distinct rooms are classified as 'Group Bookings'. Group Bookings operate under a separate amendment contract signed at inception. Unless the group leader has secured a 'Flexibility Clause' addendum, standard individual modification rules do not apply. Default Group Policy requires 14-day notice for changes; late changes incur a 50% penalty on the total value of the affected rooms.

SECTION 5: ESCALATION AND ROUTING MATRIX
All modification requests must be logged in the Central Reservation System (CRS). The system automatically routes tickets based on booking type and time-to-check-in:
- Route A (Guest Services): For Flexible Rates >72h out. No manual review needed; auto-approved.
- Route B (Revenue Management): For Flexible Rates <72h out involving rate increases. Requires manager approval to waive admin fees.
- Route C (Compliance/Legal): For Non-Refundable/Special Offer disputes. Strict adherence to Section 4.2 is mandatory. No waivers permitted by Guest Services agents.
- Route D (Group Desk): For all Group Bookings (>8 rooms). Independent of standard timing windows.

A subscriber on a month-to-month (MTM) plan may request a plan change at any time. 3.3 Effective dates
Plan changes take effect on the first day of the next billing cycle following approval, except when the request is submitted within 5 days before the end of the current billing cycle; in that case, the change takes effect on the first day of the billing cycle after the next one.

A plan change fee of $35.00 applies to all term-plan changes. No plan change fee applies to MTM plans. If a term extension is required, any promotional credits tied to the original term are forfeited.

DOCUMENT: Policy Excerpt – Refill Authorization and Early Refill Handling
Effective: 2025-01-01. Applies to all retail pharmacies in the Northlake Region.

Section 2.3 Refill Too Soon (RTS) Rule: A prescription for a maintenance medication may be refilled when at least 75% of the days supply has elapsed since the last fill date. For a 30-day supply, this means the earliest refill date is day 23. For a 90-day supply, the earliest refill date is day 68. If the patient requests a refill before the earliest date, the pharmacy must not dispense unless an override is documented (see Section 4.1).

Section 4.1 Override Reasons: A pharmacist may override the RTS rule for: (a) lost or stolen medication, with a police report or signed patient statement; (b) dose change authorized by prescriber; (c) patient traveling out of the country for more than 30 days, with itinerary; (d) manufacturer recall or product defect; (e) documented allergy to a new generic formulation. Overrides must be recorded in the pharmacy system with the reason code and supporting documentation.

Section 4.2 Quantity Limits: Controlled substances (Schedule II–V) require prescriber authorization for any early refill. No override is permitted for Schedule II except with a new written prescription and prescriber phone confirmation. Schedule III–V may be overridden for lost/stolen with a police report.

Section 5.2 Insurance and Vacation Supplies: For travel over 30 days, insurance may allow a vacation supply. If the patient’s insurance rejects a vacation supply, the pharmacy may dispense a cash-only partial fill not exceeding a 30-day supply, provided the prescriber authorizes. The RTS rule still applies to the cash fill unless an override is documented.

MEMO INTERNO DE COMPLIANCE LEGAL
De: Ana Beatriz Souza, Gerente de Compliance
Para: Equipe de Engenharia e Jurídico
Data: 14 de outubro de 2023
Assunto: Revisão de Compatibilidade de Licença - Projeto "Orbita-Core"

CONTEXTO DO PROJETO:
O projeto "Orbita-Core" é uma biblioteca de processamento de dados em tempo real desenvolvida internamente pela TechNova Ltda. A equipe de engenharia propôs a integração de duas dependências externas para acelerar o desenvolvimento do módulo de ingestão de logs. O objetivo final é distribuir o "Orbita-Core" sob a licença Apache License 2.0 (Apache-2.0), mantendo a compatibilidade com a futura incorporação da empresa por um parceiro corporativo que exige licenciamento permissivo sem obrigações de copyleft recíproco.

FATOS DO CASO E DOCUMENTAÇÃO TÉCNICA:

1. Dependência A: "FastParser"
   - Fonte: Repositório GitHub público (github.com/fastparser/lib).
   - Licença Declarada no README.md: MIT License.
   - Arquivo LICENSE.txt no repositório: Contém o texto padrão da MIT License, incluindo a cláusula de garantia limitada.
   - Observação da Equipe de Segurança: Em 05/10/2023, um scanner automatizado identificou uma linha de código comentada no arquivo `src/parser.c` que diz: // TODO: Migrar para GPL v3 para garantir liberdade de software. Esta linha foi removida na versão 1.2.0 lançada em 10/10/2023. A versão utilizada pelo Orbita-Core é a 1.2.0.
   - Status de Conformidade: Aprovado preliminarmente pelo scanner SCA (Software Composition Analysis) como MIT.

2. Dependência B: "SecureHasher"
   - Fonte: Distribuição Linux Debian (pacote stable).
   - Licença Declarada no changelog.dch: GNU General Public License version 2 (GPL-2.0-only).
   - Análise do Jurídico Externo (Escritório Silva & Mendes):
     - Relatório datado de 12/10/2023 afirma que o código-fonte da SecureHasher contém trechos derivados do projeto "LibCrypto", que possui licença LGPL-2.1.
     - A análise aponta que a compilação estática (linkagem estática) da SecureHasher dentro do binário final do Orbita-Core cria um trabalho derivado único.
     - O parecer jurídico conclui que a distribuição do binário final contendo a linkagem estática da SecureHasher viola os termos da GPL-2.0 se não for acompanhado do código-fonte completo do Orbita-Core sob a mesma licença GPL-2.0 ou compatible.
     - Alternativa sugerida pelo parecer: Linkagem dinâmica via shared library (.so) pode evitar a criação de trabalho derivado, mas depende da interpretação específica sobre "combinação" vs "derivação".

3. Restrições Corporativas da TechNova:
   - Política P-09: Proíbe a incorporação de qualquer código sob licenças copyleft forte (como GPL v2 ou v3) em produtos finais destinados à venda ou distribuição pública, a menos que o produto inteiro seja relicenciado sob a mesma licença copyleft.
   - Política P-10: Permite licenças permissivas (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0) sem restrição, desde que não haja conflito direto entre as condições de redistribuição.

DISCUSSÃO EM THREAD DE EMAIL (EXCERTO):

[De: Carlos Eduardo (Engenheiro Chefe)]
Carlos, você confirmou que o FastParser não tem riscos devido ao comentário TODO? Isso parece ser apenas um erro de digitação ou nota antiga, não muda a licença MIT oficial do arquivo LICENSE, certo?

[Para: Marina Lopes (DevOps)]
Marina, sobre o SecureHasher, notei que estamos fazendo build estático por padrão para facilitar o deploy em containers Alpine Linux. Se mudarmos para dinâmico, precisamos alterar o Dockerfile e testar a performance. Vale a pena o risco legal?

[De: Fernanda Costa (Jurídico)]
Fernanda, o relatório do escritório Silva & Mendes é definitivo? Eles consideram a linkagem estática como incompatível com Apache-2.0? Lembro que a FSF já disse que linkagem estática gera obra derivada.

[Resposta de Fernanda Costa]
O relatório indica que a incompatibilidade existe especificamente porque o Orbita-Core seria distribuído sob Apache-2.0. A GPL-2.0 impõe que trabalhos derivados sejam licenciados sob GPL. Como o Orbita-Core usa Apache-2.0, há um conflito de termos de patente e copyleft. A única forma segura de usar SecureHasher hoje é abandonar a estratégia de linkagem estática OU abandonar a intenção de manter a licença Apache-2.0 no produto final, optando por GPL-2.0. Não podemos fazer ambos.

LOG DO PIPELINE CI/CD (JENKINS) - BUILD #452:
- Data: 13/10/2023
- Etapa: Dependency Check
- Resultado: SUCCESS
- Nota: Scanner ignorou alerta de "Potencial Violação de Licença" para SecureHasher pois a regra estava configurada como 'warning' e não 'error'.
- Artefato gerado: orbita-core-static.tar.gz (tamanho: 45MB)

PEDIDO DE DECISÃO:
Precisamos definir a estratégia de lançamento para a versão 1.0 do Orbita-Core até sexta-feira, 20/10/2023.

criteria.false: Não, a licença vigente é MIT conforme o arquivo LICENSE e a versão usada não contém o trecho problemático ativo.

Effective for reservations booked on or after 1 March 2025.

1. Definitions. "Arrival date" means the first night of the reservation. "Change" means altering dates, room type, rate plan, or guest name. "Cancellation" means removing the entire stay. "Peak period" means 20 December through 3 January inclusive, plus 1 May through 5 May inclusive.

2. Standard rate change rules. For reservations on the Standard Flexible rate:
- A change made 14 or more days before the arrival date is free, subject to availability and any rate difference.
- A change made 7 to 13 days before the arrival date costs USD 75, plus any rate difference.
- A change made 6 days or fewer before the arrival date costs one night's room charge, plus any rate difference.
- Once the arrival date has passed, no change is permitted; the reservation is treated as a no-show unless checked in.

3. Non-refundable Advance rate. Changes to an Advance rate booking are not allowed. Cancellation forfeits 100% of the prepaid amount. Name corrections (spelling only, same guest) are allowed at no charge at any time before check-in.

4. Peak period exception. Any change to a stay that includes at least one peak-period night costs USD 150 regardless of how far in advance the change is requested, and the 14-day free window does not apply. Peak-period changes also require the rate difference to be paid.

5. Group bookings (10 or more rooms). Changes require 30 days' written notice and are handled by the Group Desk; the rules above do not apply.

6. Administrative fee. A USD 25 administrative fee applies to every permitted change, except name corrections and changes to Advance rate bookings, which are not permitted. The USD 25 fee is included in, not added to, the USD 75, USD 150, and one-night charges described above.

Aplicável a todos os eventos da produtora Horizonte Cultural Ltda., CNPJ 12.345.678/0001-90.

1. DEFINIÇÕES
1.1 Titular: pessoa física que consta como comprador no sistema de vendas.
1.2 Portador: pessoa física que apresenta o ingresso na entrada.
1.3 Transferência: cessão definitiva do ingresso a terceiro, alterando o portador no sistema.
1.4 Cessão temporária: empréstimo do ingresso por prazo determinado, sem alteração cadastral.

2. REGRAS GERAIS
2.1 A transferência definitiva só é permitida até 72 horas antes do início do evento.
2.2 O titular pode transferir cada ingresso no máximo duas vezes.
2.3 É vedada a transferência de ingressos de cortesia, imprensa, meia-entrada e de setores com controle nominal.
2.4 A taxa de transferência é de R$ 35,00 por ingresso, paga pelo titular no ato da solicitação.
2.5 A transferência só se conclui após confirmação por e-mail enviada ao novo portador e aceite deste em até 48 horas.
2.6 Não há reembolso da taxa em caso de não comparecimento do novo portador.

3. CASOS EXCEPCIONAIS
3.1 Em caso de impedimento por força maior (doença grave, luto, convocação judicial), o titular pode solicitar transferência fora do prazo mediante envio de documentação comprobatória em até 24 horas após o evento.
3.2 A análise excepcional é feita pelo setor de Relacionamento e leva até 5 dias úteis.
3.3 Se aprovada, a transferência excepcional não altera a contagem de transferências já realizadas.

4. EVENTOS COM REGRAS ESPECÍFICAS
4.1 O Festival Aurora Boreal, realizado em 12/07/2025, no Estádio Municipal de Belo Horizonte, possui regulamento próprio.
4.2 Para o Festival Aurora Boreal, a transferência definitiva é permitida até 24 horas antes do evento, e a taxa é de R$ 50,00.
4.3 Os ingressos do Festival Aurora Boreal são nominais e exigem documento oficial com foto na entrada.
4.4 O setor Arquibancada Norte do Festival Aurora Boreal é destinado exclusivamente a maiores de 18 anos.

5. FATOS DO CASO

S3 — Médio: degradação perceptível sem perda de transação; indisponibilidade de serviço não essencial; OU impacto entre 50 e 500 usuários.
S4 — Baixo: incidente sem impacto em usuários finais, apenas em ambiente de homologação ou em ferramentas internas de baixa criticidade.

Art. 6º O prazo de primeira resposta (SLA) é de 15 min para S1, 30 min para S2, 4 h para S3 e 1 dia útil para S4, contados da abertura do chamado.

CONFIDENTIAL: INTERNAL MEMO - BOOKING CHANGE POLICY UPDATE
Date: October 12, 2024
From: Revenue Management Team
To: Front Desk Operations
Subject: Clarification on Flexible vs. Standard Rate Modifications

1. STANDARD RATE TERMS
All bookings marked 'Standard' are non-refundable after the check-in date passes. Changes to dates or room types are permitted only if the new total cost is equal to or higher than the original booking. If the new cost is lower, no credit is issued, and the difference is forfeited. A flat administrative fee of $50 applies to any modification made less than 72 hours before the scheduled arrival time.

2. FLEXIBLE RATE TERMS
Bookings marked 'Flexible' allow free cancellation up to 48 hours prior to arrival. After this window, a penalty equivalent to one night's stay applies for cancellations. For modifications (changing dates/rooms), no administrative fee is charged regardless of timing. However, if the modification results in a higher total cost, the guest must pay the difference plus a mandatory 12% service charge on the increased amount. If the modification results in a lower total cost, the difference is refunded to the original payment method within 5-7 business days, provided the request is made at least 24 hours before the new arrival date. Requests for refunds on price reductions made fewer than 24 hours before arrival are denied, and the original higher rate stands.

3. CROSS-POLICY RESTRICTIONS
A booking cannot be converted from Standard to Flexible status post-booking without paying the full difference in base rate plus a $75 conversion fee. Conversely, downgrading from Flexible to Standard requires a minimum 7-day notice period before the first night of the original booking. 

CASE FACTS:
Guest Name: Elena Rostova
Confirmation Number: #HR-9921-B
Original Booking Date Created: November 1, 2024
Original Arrival Date: December 20, 2024
Original Departure Date: December 23, 2024 (3 nights)
Original Rate Type: Flexible
Original Total Cost: $600 ($200/night + taxes already included in displayed total for simplicity)

EVENT LOG:
[Dec 19, 10:00 AM] Guest calls to modify reservation. She requests to change departure date to December 21, 2024 (reducing stay to 1 night) due to a sudden work emergency. Current system calculates new total cost as $200. The agent notes that since the new cost ($200) is lower than the original ($600), a refund of $400 should be processed. However, the policy states refunds for price reductions are only allowed if requested at least 24 hours before the NEW arrival date. The NEW arrival date remains December 20, 2024. The call was made on December 19 at 10:00 AM. The time difference between Dec 19, 10:00 AM and Dec 20, 12:00 PM (standard noon cutoff) is approximately 26 hours. Wait, the policy says "before the new arrival date." Usually, arrival dates are calendar days. Let's look at the specific clause: "provided the request is made at least 24 hours before the new arrival date." In hotel systems, "arrival date" often implies the start of the day (00:00). If we interpret strictly by calendar date, Dec 19 is more than 24 hours before Dec 20? No, Dec 19 10AM to Dec 20 00:00 is 14 hours. This is critical.

Let's re-read the timestamp carefully. 
Request Time: Dec 19, 10:00 AM.
New Arrival Date: Dec 20.
Is the request at least 24 hours before the New Arrival Date?
If "New Arrival Date" means the beginning of Dec 20 (midnight), then Dec 19 10:00 AM is only 14 hours prior. Therefore, the condition "at least 24 hours before" is NOT met.

Agent Action: Agent denies the refund of the $400 difference based on the timing clause. Agent confirms the stay will now be billed at the original $600 rate because the modification resulted in a lower cost but was requested too late for a refund adjustment, effectively keeping the original high charge despite the shorter stay.

Front Desk (Mark): "Dear Ms. Rostova, per our Flexible Terms, Section 2, while you can modify the dates, refunds for price reductions are only granted if the request is received at least 24 hours prior to the new arrival date. Your request came in on Dec 19 at 10 AM. The new arrival date is Dec 20. Assuming standard midnight cutoffs, this is less than 24 hours. Thus, the original rate holds."
Guest (Elena): "But what about the cancellation penalty? I didn't cancel, I modified."

Seção 3. Classificação de gravidade e prazos
3.1 Toda denúncia recebe uma classificação de gravidade, de G1 (menor) a G4 (maior), conforme a natureza do conteúdo e o risco associado.
3.2 Prazos máximos de análise contados a partir do registro da denúncia:
- G1: 10 dias úteis, sem remoção cautelar.
- G2: 5 dias úteis, sem remoção cautelar.
- G3: 48 horas corridas, com remoção cautelar imediata quando o conteúdo estiver público.
- G4: 4 horas corridas, com remoção cautelar imediata e escalonamento ao Comitê de Integridade.
3.3 São G4: conteúdo que envolva risco iminente de morte ou integridade física; exploração sexual de menores; incentivo direto a violência coletiva.
3.4 São G3: assédio direcionado e reiterado; discurso de ódio contra grupo protegido; divulgação de dados pessoais sensíveis (doxxing) de pessoa privada; ameaça velada.
3.5 São G2: desinformação sobre saúde com potencial de dano; golpes financeiros sem vítima identificada; conteúdo sexual não consentido envolvendo adultos.
3.6 São G1: linguagem ofensiva isolada sem alvo determinado; spam comercial; conteúdo potencialmente enganoso de baixo impacto.
3.7 Se houver mais de um enquadramento possível, aplica-se sempre o de maior gravidade.

Seção 5. Agravantes e atenuantes
5.1 Agravam a classificação em um nível: conteúdo direcionado a menor de idade; reincidência do autor nos últimos 90 dias; uso de conta recém-criada (menos de 7 dias) para veicular o conteúdo.
5.2 Atenuam a classificação em um nível: conteúdo publicado em perfil privado com menos de 50 seguidores; autor que removeu espontaneamente o conteúdo antes da denúncia.
5.3 Nunca se aplica mais de um agravante ou mais de um atenuante ao mesmo caso; se houver dois agravantes, conta-se apenas um.
5.4 Um agravante e um atenuante simultâneos se cancelam, retornando à classificação original.

Seção 8. Remoção cautelar
8.1 A remoção cautelar é obrigatória para G3 e G4 quando o conteúdo estiver público.
8.2 Para G1 e G2, a remoção só ocorre após decisão final.
8.3 A remoção cautelar não implica decisão final; a análise deve prosseguir no prazo da classificação.

Seção 11. Registro
11.1 O registro da denúncia se dá no momento em que o formulário é enviado, não quando é lido.
11.2 Denúncias registradas fora do horário comercial (após 18h ou em fins de semana) começam a contar o prazo no primeiro dia útil seguinte.

Section 4.2 Customer Identification Program (CIP) – Individual Accounts
4.2.1 Primary identification documents accepted for U.S. persons: unexpired state-issued driver’s license, U.S. passport, or U.S. passport card. For non-U.S. persons: unexpired foreign passport with valid U.S. visa or I-94, or unexpired permanent resident card (Form I-551).
4.2.2 Secondary evidence: utility bill, bank statement, or government correspondence dated within the last 60 days showing the customer’s name and residential address. PO boxes are not acceptable as residential address.
4.2.3 Name matching: The name on the primary ID must match the name provided on the application exactly, ignoring middle name or initial, suffix (Jr., Sr., III), and case. A hyphenated surname may be matched as either hyphenated or separated by a space. Nicknames are not acceptable unless supported by secondary evidence.
4.2.4 Address matching: The residential address on the application must match the address on secondary evidence or the primary ID. If the primary ID shows an old address, secondary evidence is required. If secondary evidence is a bank statement, it must be from a U.S. financial institution.
4.2.5 Expiration: An expired primary ID is not acceptable. If the ID expired within the last 30 days, a renewal receipt from the issuing authority may be accepted as temporary proof, provided the receipt shows the same name and date of birth. Otherwise, the application must be pended for a valid ID.
4.2.6 Document quality: Photocopies, screenshots, or digital images are acceptable if all security features, text, and photo are clearly legible. Redacted documents are not acceptable unless the redaction is only of a Social Security Number.

MERIDIAN UNIVERSITY FINANCIAL AID POLICY EXCERPT: GRADUATE MERIT SCHOLARSHIP (GMS) ELIGIBILITY
Effective Date: August 1, 2023
Last Updated: June 15, 2024

SECTION 1: ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA
To qualify for the Graduate Merit Scholarship (GMS), a student must meet ALL of the following conditions simultaneously at the time of application:
1.1 Academic Standing: The applicant must be enrolled in a full-time graduate program (minimum 9 credit hours per semester). Part-time enrollment is strictly ineligible.
1.2 GPA Requirement: The cumulative Grade Point Average (GPA) on a 4.0 scale must be 3.75 or higher as of the end of the most recently completed semester. Transfer credits are included in the calculation if evaluated by the Registrar.
1.3 Financial Need Verification: While primarily merit-based, applicants must have submitted their Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) to the university by the priority deadline. Applications without a FAFSA record are automatically disqualified.
1.4 Enrollment Status: Applicants cannot hold any other federal or state-funded scholarship that exceeds $5,000 per academic year. Institutional awards do not count toward this cap unless specified in Section 1.5.
1.5 Stacking Rule: If an applicant receives a partial GMS award, they may retain up to $2,000 of another institutional grant. Any amount above $2,000 from other institutional sources must be reduced proportionally from the GMS award to maintain total aid parity.

SECTION 2: APPLICATION PROCESS AND DEADLINES
2.1 Priority Deadline: All applications and supporting documents must be received by the Financial Aid Office no later than March 1st for the upcoming Fall semester.
2.2 Late Submission: Applications received after March 1st are considered only if funds remain. No guarantees are made regarding late submissions.
2.3 Documentation: Applicants must provide an official transcript and a signed FAFSA confirmation page.

INTERNAL POLICY EXCERPT: WAREHOUSE INVENTORY VARIANCE PROTOCOL (WIVP-2024)

1. DEFINITION OF VARIANCE TYPES:
   - Type A (Systemic): Discrepancy caused by software error, barcode scanning failure, or receipt processing glitch.
   - Type B (Operational): Discrepancy caused by physical handling errors, such as picking the wrong SKU, mislabeling, or damage during transit within the warehouse.
   - Type C (Security/Loss): Unexplained disappearance of high-value items (> $500/unit) or evidence of theft.

2. ROUTING DECISION MATRIX:
   - If Variance Type is A: Route to IT Support Ticket Queue for root cause analysis.
   - If Variance Type is B AND Value < $1,000: Route to Warehouse Operations Supervisor for immediate cycle count adjustment and staff retraining.
   - If Variance Type is B AND Value >= $1,000: Route to Loss Prevention & Compliance Team for investigation.
   - If Variance Type is C: Route immediately to Security Department and Regional Director.
   - IF CAUSE IS UNKNOWN AFTER INITIAL REVIEW: Route to Inventory Control Analyst for deep-dive audit.

3. THRESHOLDS:
   - High-Value Threshold for routing escalation: $1,000 total variance value.
   - Cycle Count Frequency: Weekly for A-items; Monthly for B/C-items.

Date: October 15, 2023
From: Sarah Jenkins, Director of Quality Control
To: Production Managers, Supply Chain Lead
Subject: Revised Criteria for Non-Conforming Material (NCM) Release

Policy Overview:
Materials flagged with a 'Quality Hold' status must undergo a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) before release. The release decision tree depends on the severity of the defect and the origin of the batch.

1. Minor Defects (Cosmetic/Non-Functional): If the defect is classified as 'Minor' in the Supplier Corrective Action Request (SCAR) log, the batch may be released via 'Concession' if it meets all safety standards. Concession requires approval from both the Quality Manager (QM) and the Product Owner (PO). No RCA is required for minor defects if historical pass rates exceed 98%.

2. Major Defects (Functional/Safety): If the defect is 'Major', an RCA is mandatory. The RCA report must be reviewed by the Chief Engineer (CE). Release is permitted only if the CE signs off on the 'Corrective Action Effectiveness'. If the defect originated from a Tier 1 supplier, a full audit is required before any subsequent batches are accepted. If the defect originated internally, a process deviation investigation is required instead of a supplier audit.

3. Critical Defects: Any defect affecting regulatory compliance or immediate user safety results in automatic scrap. No release is possible under any condition.

DOCUMENT: Reservation & Cancellation Policy Excerpt — The Willow & Vine (Effective January 1, 2025)

SECTION 2. STANDARD RESERVATION TERMS
2.1 A reservation for a standard table (parties of 1–6) is confirmed upon receipt of a $25 per-person deposit, charged at booking.
2.2 Deposits are fully refundable if the reservation is cancelled at least 48 hours before the scheduled seating time.
2.3 Cancellations made 24–48 hours before the seating time forfeit 50% of the deposit.
2.4 Cancellations made less than 24 hours before the seating time, or no-shows, forfeit the full deposit.
2.5 A no-show is recorded if the party has not arrived within 20 minutes of the scheduled seating time and has not contacted the restaurant.

SECTION 3. LARGE PARTIES (7 OR MORE)
3.1 Large-party reservations require a $50 per-person deposit and a signed event agreement.
3.2 For large parties, cancellation 7 or more days before the seating time results in a full refund.
3.3 Cancellation 3–6 days before the seating time forfeits 50% of the deposit.
3.4 Cancellation fewer than 3 days before the seating time forfeits the full deposit.

SECTION 4. EXCEPTIONS AND OVERRIDES
4.1 Medical Emergency Override: If a guest cancels due to a documented medical emergency (hospital admission, emergency room visit, or physician-ordered quarantine), the full deposit is refunded regardless of Sections 2.3, 2.4, 3.3, or 3.4. The guest must provide documentation within 5 business days of the scheduled seating time. This override applies to both standard and large-party reservations.
4.2 Severe Weather Override: If the National Weather Service has issued a Severe Thunderstorm Warning, Tornado Warning, or Winter Storm Warning for the restaurant's county at any time during the 6 hours preceding the scheduled seating time, any cancellation or no-show is treated as a timely cancellation under Section 2.2 (or Section 3.2 for large parties), and the full deposit is refunded. Documentation is not required for this override.
4.3 Private Room Buyouts: Buyouts are governed solely by the signed event agreement and are not eligible for the overrides in 4.1 or 4.2.

SECTION 5. RESCHEDULING
5.1 A reservation may be rescheduled once at no cost if the request is made at least 48 hours (standard) or 7 days (large party) before the seating time. The deposit carries over to the new date.
5.2 If the rescheduled date is later cancelled, the cancellation policy is applied based on the original booking date's deposit terms.

PARECER NORMATIVO Nº 042/2024 — ASSUNTO: LIMITES DE ALÇADA PARA APROVAÇÃO DE DESPESAS E COMPRAS

Art. 1º Esta norma disciplina a aprovação de despesas de custeio e investimento no âmbito da Administração Direta, observados os limites abaixo:
I — até R$ 8.000,00 (oito mil reais): aprovação pelo Coordenador da unidade requisitante;
II — de R$ 8.000,01 até R$ 40.000,00: aprovação pelo Diretor da área requisitante;
III — de R$ 40.000,01 até R$ 150.000,00: aprovação pelo Secretário da pasta;
IV — acima de R$ 150.000,00: aprovação pelo Prefeito, após parecer prévio da Comissão Permanente de Licitação.
Parágrafo único. Para fins de enquadramento, considera-se o valor total da contratação, incluindo prorrogações, aditivos e despesas acessórias estimadas.

Art. 2º As compras de bens permanentes classificadas como investimento seguem os mesmos limites do art. 1º, mas exigem, em qualquer hipótese, registro patrimonial prévio e parecer da Divisão de Patrimônio.

Art. 3º Em caso de fracionamento de despesa vedado, a autoridade competente deve consolidar as contratações do mesmo objeto no exercício financeiro para fins de alçada.

Art. 4º Despesas de urgência comprovada podem ser autorizadas pelo Secretário da pasta, independentemente do valor, desde que ratificadas pelo Prefeito em até 5 (cinco) dias úteis, sob pena de nulidade.

Art. 5º Esta norma entra em vigor na data de sua publicação, revogadas as disposições em contrário.

MEMORANDUM: 2024 Simplified Home Office Deduction Rules
From: Internal Compliance Team
Date: October 15, 2024
Subject: Updated Guidelines for Remote Work Expense Claims

Section 1: Eligibility Criteria
To qualify for the Standard Deduction Method (flat rate), an employee must satisfy all of the following conditions:
1. The employee must have worked from home for a minimum of 60 days during the fiscal year.
2. The home office space must be used exclusively for work purposes at least 80% of the time.
3. The employee must not have received any employer-provided workspace in the past 12 months.

If an employee fails to meet ANY of the criteria in Section 1, they are ineligible for the Standard Deduction. However, they may still apply for the Itemized Deduction Method if they can prove that their total eligible expenses exceed $1,200 and that at least one expense was incurred specifically for maintaining the dedicated workspace (e.g., repairs, specialized furniture).

Section 2: Expense Definitions
Eligible Expenses for Itemized Calculation include:
- Internet service plans with a minimum speed of 100 Mbps.
- Electricity costs attributable solely to the workspace equipment (must be estimated using a sub-meter or approved calculator tool; general household bills are not eligible unless split by square footage AND equipment usage hours).
- Ergonomic chairs purchased after January 1, 2024.

If a meter reading is estimated rather than actual, the difference between the estimated charge and the subsequent actual reading will be credited or debited in the next billing cycle. Customers are eligible for a flat $50 credit if power is interrupted for more than 8 hours during severe weather events, provided the interruption was not caused by internal wiring faults within the customer's premises. A política abaixo se aplica a todas as reservas feitas por telefone, e-mail, site ou aplicativo, para o período de 1º de janeiro de 2024 a 31 de dezembro de 2024.

1. RESERVAS

1.2. A reserva é confirmada somente após o envio do e-mail de confirmação pela equipe do restaurante.

1.4. Reservas para datas especiais (véspera de Natal, Natal, Réveillon, Dia dos Namorados, Dia das Mães) exigem cartão de crédito para garantia.

2. CANCELAMENTO PELO CLIENTE
2.1. Cancelamentos com mais de 24 horas de antecedência do horário reservado não geram cobrança.
2.2. Cancelamentos entre 24 e 4 horas de antecedência geram cobrança de R$ 50,00 por pessoa.
2.3. Cancelamentos com menos de 4 horas de antecedência ou não comparecimento (no-show) geram cobrança de R$ 90,00 por pessoa.
2.4. Para reservas com garantia de cartão de crédito, o valor cobrado é o mesmo das regras acima, acrescido de 10% de taxa administrativa.

2.6. O cancelamento deve ser feito pelo mesmo canal da reserva ou pelo e-mail reservas@saborarte.com.br.

3. ALTERAÇÕES
3.1. Alterações de data ou horário podem ser feitas sem custo com até 24 horas de antecedência, sujeitas à disponibilidade.
3.2. Alterações com menos de 24 horas de antecedência são tratadas como cancelamento e nova reserva.

4. NO-SHOW
4.1. Considera-se no-show a não apresentação do cliente em até 15 minutos após o horário reservado, sem aviso prévio.

5.1. O restaurante não se responsabiliza por objetos esquecidos no local.

**INTERNAL MEMORANDUM: REFILL AUTHORIZATION POLICY (REV. 2024-10)**

**1. Eligibility Criteria for Early Refills**
Standard refills are permitted only when the patient has consumed at least 90% of the previous supply. An "Early Refill" is defined as a request made prior to the standard eligibility date. Early refills may be authorized under the following conditions:
   a) **Emergency Supply**: A single 3-day emergency supply is permitted without prescriber contact if the medication is non-controlled and the patient presents with an urgent need.
   b) **Travel Authorization**: Patients traveling more than 75 miles from their residence for longer than 7 days may receive a full 30-day early refill, provided they submit a signed travel affidavit and proof of itinerary.
   c) **Prescriber Override**: If a prescriber explicitly authorizes an early refill via secure fax or encrypted email, the pharmacy may dispense up to the amount specified by the prescriber, not exceeding a 60-day supply total per calendar month for maintenance medications.

**2. Controlled Substance Restrictions**
Schedule II-V medications cannot be issued as Emergency Supplies. Schedule III-V medications require a valid prescription on file and cannot utilize the Travel Authorization provision; they strictly follow the 90% consumption rule unless a Prescriber Override is documented.

**3. Documentation Requirements**
All early refills must be logged in the Patient Management System (PMS). For Prescriber Overrides, the electronic communication timestamp must match within 24 hours of dispensing. For Travel Authorizations, the affidavit must be scanned into the PMS before dispensing.

[Policy Excerpt — Effective 2025-01-01]

Section 3.1: Standard Appointments
- Routine check-ups: may be booked up to 90 days in advance.
- Urgent same-day appointments: reserved for patients with acute symptoms (e.g., fever > 101°F, severe pain, shortness of breath).
- Follow-up visits: must be scheduled within 14 days of a prior visit unless the treating provider specifies a longer interval in the chart.

Section 3.2: Cancellations and No-Shows
- Patients who cancel with less than 24 hours' notice are charged a $25 late-cancellation fee.
- Patients who do not show up for a scheduled appointment are charged a $40 no-show fee.
- A patient who accumulates three no-shows within 12 months is placed on a 30-day scheduling restriction, during which they may only book same-day urgent appointments.
- Waivers: Fees and restrictions may be waived only if the patient provides documentation of an emergency (e.g., hospital admission, death in family) within 7 days of the missed appointment. The waiver is not automatic; it must be approved by the clinic manager.

Section 3.3: Provider-Specific Rules
- Dr. Alvarez: does not accept new patients for routine check-ups; only sees established patients and urgent cases.
- Dr. Chen: sees patients of all ages, but requires a referral for any appointment longer than 30 minutes.
- Dr. Okafor: pediatric patients only (under 18).
- Dr. Singh: accepts new patients, but only for urgent same-day appointments.

Section 3.4: Insurance and Payment
- Appointments cannot be confirmed until insurance is verified. Self-pay patients must pay a $50 deposit at booking.
- If insurance verification fails, the appointment is held for 48 hours; if not resolved, it is cancelled.

Section 3.5: Overbooking and Waitlist
- Providers may be overbooked by no more than 2 patients per half-day session.
- Waitlist patients are offered cancellations in order of urgency, then by date added to waitlist.

Section 14.2.3: Lot Coverage and Setbacks
All residential additions must maintain a minimum rear setback of 15 feet from the property line. The total lot coverage for single-family zones cannot exceed 40% of the total lot area. Section 14.2.9: Structural Review Requirements
A licensed structural engineer’s stamp is required for:
1. Additions exceeding 200 square feet.
2. Any modification to load-bearing walls, regardless of size.
3. Projects involving foundation underpinning or deep excavation within 5 feet of existing foundations.
Note: Cosmetic changes (painting, flooring replacement) do not require engineering stamps unless they involve structural framing changes.

Section 14.3.1: Permit Application Routing
Applications are routed based on complexity and risk factors:
- Tier 1 (Over-the-Counter): Additions <100 sq ft, no structural changes, within setback limits. Approved same day.
- Tier 2 (Standard Review): Additions 100–200 sq ft with minor non-load-bearing adjustments; OR additions >200 sq ft without structural modifications if all setbacks are met. Review time: 5 business days.
- Tier 3 (Comprehensive Review): Any project requiring a variance; OR any project with structural engineering requirements; OR any project affecting drainage or utility easements. Review time: 15–20 business days.
- Tier 4 (Special Committee): Projects in historic districts or those with significant environmental impact assessments.

SECTION 14.4: Fee Schedule
Tier 1: $150

INTERNAL MEMO: LEGAL COMPLIANCE REVIEW
Date: October 14, 2023
From: Sarah Jenkins, Senior Legal Counsel
To: DevOps Lead, Engineering Team
Subject: License Compatibility Assessment for Project 'Nexus-Core' Release v2.1.0

CONTEXT
The Engineering team has requested a final legal clearance for the upcoming release of Nexus-Core v2.1.0. The project is intended to be distributed under the MIT License. However, during dependency scanning, several third-party libraries were identified that may introduce incompatible licensing obligations. This memo outlines the specific components in question and their license statuses as verified by our automated tooling and manual review.

COMPONENT ANALYSIS

1. lib-fast-json (v3.4.2)
   - Detected License: Apache-2.0
   - Status: Compatible with MIT distribution when used as a standalone library linked dynamically. The Apache-2.0 patent grant clause does not conflict with MIT's permissive nature for this use case. No attribution notice is required in the source code comments beyond standard NOTICE file inclusion if redistributed in binary form. We have confirmed the upstream repository maintains a valid NOTICE file.

2. secure-crypto-wrapper (v1.0.5)
   - Detected License: GPL-3.0-only
   - Status: Incompatible. The Nexus-Core project intends to remain under MIT. Linking statically or dynamically against a GPL-3.0 component generally triggers copyleft provisions, requiring the entire derivative work to be licensed under GPL-3.0. Since we do not wish to relicense Nexus-Core, this dependency must be removed or replaced with an MIT-compatible alternative (e.g., OpenSSL which is Apache-2.0/MIT dual). Note: There was a previous claim that version 1.0.4 was LGPL, but manual inspection of the header files confirms 1.0.5 is strictly GPL-3.0-only. It is NOT true that this component lacks any copyleft restrictions.

3. data-parser-util (v2.2.0)
   - Detected License: ISC
   - Status: Compatible. The ISC license is functionally equivalent to the BSD-2-Clause license and is widely considered compatible with MIT. No additional action is required.

4. legacy-auth-module (v0.9.1)
   - Detected License: Proprietary / Commercial EULA
   - Status: Incompatible for open-source distribution. Our contract with the vendor, AuthSecure Inc., explicitly prohibits redistribution of the compiled binaries in an open-source package without a separate commercial sublicense fee of $5,000/month. We have not secured this budget. Therefore, this module cannot be included in the public GitHub repository. It must be excluded from the build pipeline entirely.

POLICY EXCERPT (Section 4.2: Derivative Works)
"If a project includes any component licensed under a strong copyleft license (such as GPL-2.0-or-later or GPL-3.0), the resulting combined work must be licensed under the same or a compatible copyleft license. Permissive licenses like MIT and Apache-2.0 are generally compatible with each other unless specific patent retaliation clauses create friction, which they do not in standard usage patterns. Dual-licensed components require verification of which license branch was selected at compile time."

EMAIL THREAD FRAGMENT
From: Mike Ross <mross@company.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins
Date: Oct 12, 2023
Hi Sarah,
We found a workaround for the secure-crypto-wrapper issue. If we isolate it behind a plugin interface loaded at runtime rather than linking at compile time, can we avoid the GPL contagion?
Best,
Mike

Reply from Sarah:
No, Mike. Runtime loading does not absolve copyright infringement if the core program depends on the GPL code to function fundamentally. Unless the main program can run meaningfully without the plugin, it is a derivative work. Please remove the dependency.

ACTION REQUIRED
Engineering must exclude `secure-crypto-wrapper` and `legacy-auth-module` from the v2.1.0 artifact before merging to main.

Subject: Three-Way Match and Payment Release Protocols

1. MATCHING CRITERIA
A payment is eligible for automatic release only if all three conditions are met:
a) The Purchase Order (PO) quantity matches the Invoice quantity exactly.
b) The Unit Price on the Invoice matches the Unit Price on the PO exactly.
c) The Total Amount on the Invoice matches the calculated total (Quantity * Unit Price) plus any pre-approved Freight/Tax codes listed in the PO header.

2. PAYMENT TERMS AND DATES
Standard Net 30 terms apply unless specified otherwise on the PO. 
Discount Logic: If 'Early Pay Discount' is enabled on the vendor master file, payments made within 15 days of invoice date qualify for a 2% discount deduction from the gross amount. Payments after day 15 but before day 30 pay the full gross amount. Payments after day 30 incur late fees.
Holiday Adjustment: If the due date falls on a weekend or federal holiday, the due date shifts to the next business day. Federal holidays observed by the company: New Year's Day, MLK Day, Presidents' Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day, Veterans Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas.

3. EXCEPTION HANDLING
Discrepancies under $5.00 may be written off automatically by the system if the reason code 'ROUNDING' is selected. Discrepancies over $5.00 require Manager Approval via Ticket System.

INTERNAL MEMORANDUM: GLOBAL LOGISTICS POLICY GL-2024-09
Subject: Customs Clearance Protocols for High-Value Industrial Machinery Imports
Effective Date: October 1, 2024

1. GENERAL VALUATION RULE
All imported goods must be declared at their transaction value (FOB price). For machinery exceeding $50,000 USD in value, a certified appraisal from an approved vendor list (AVL) is mandatory before entry filing. The standard duty rate for HS Code 8479.89 is 4.5%.

2. EXCEPTION: TEMPORARY IMPORT BOND PROCEDURE
Under specific circumstances, the AVL appraisal requirement may be waived if the importer qualifies for the Temporary Import Bond (TIB) procedure under Section 321 of the Tariff Act. To qualify for this exception:
a. The equipment must be designated as 'Rental' or 'Leased' with a confirmed return date within 12 months.
b. A TIB bond equal to 150% of the estimated duty and taxes must be posted by a surety company recognized by CBP.
c. The waiver applies ONLY if the bonded amount covers the full potential liability.
d. If the equipment is sold domestically or fails to leave the country within 12 months, the waiver is retroactively voided, and penalties apply.

3. PROCESSING TIMELINES AND SLA
Standard processing time for TIB waivers is 5 business days after receipt of all documentation. Expedited processing (2 business days) incurs a $500 surcharge.

From: Sarah Jenkins, Senior Counsel

Subject: Clarification on Apache License 2.0 vs GPLv3 Interaction

Current Policy (v2.1, effective Jan 2022): The 'One-Way Street' rule applies. Code under the GNU General Public License version 3 (GPLv3) may be linked with code under the Apache License 2.0. However, combined works distributed as a single binary must comply with GPLv3 terms, which includes providing source code and preserving copyleft. POLICY EXCERPT: SECTION 4.2 - VIOLENT GRAPHIC CONTENT AND HATE SPEECH THRESHOLDS

4.2.1 Definition of Violent Graphic Content (VGC):
Any media depicting severe physical injury, death, or dismemberment is classified as VGC if the content is primarily intended to shock, harass, or intimidate. However, educational, documentary, scientific, or artistic (EDSA) contexts are exempt from removal IF the depiction is necessary for the context and not gratuitous.

4.2.2 Definition of Hate Speech:
Content that dehumanizes individuals based on protected attributes (race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disability) by comparing them to animals, diseases, or sub-human entities. This includes slurs used in a derogatory manner. Reclaimed terms used within the community to which they belong are NOT considered hate speech.

4.2.3 The "Gratuitousness" Test:
To determine if VGC is exempt under EDSA, moderators must apply the Gratuitousness Test. If the graphic violence is included solely for shock value, titillation, or to amplify fear without providing substantive informational value, it is NOT exempt. If the violence is essential to convey the historical or scientific reality being discussed, it IS exempt.

DISPUTE RESOLUTION POLICY (EXCERPT)
Effective January 1, 2024

Section 4.2 – Billing Adjustments for Metering Errors
A customer may request a billing adjustment if they believe their meter is inaccurate. The utility will conduct a meter test within 15 business days of a written request. If the meter is found to be outside the acceptable accuracy range (registering more than 2% fast or slow), the utility will adjust the bill for the current billing period and the immediately preceding billing period only. Adjustments beyond two periods require evidence of a chronic defect documented by a utility technician.

Section 4.5 – Estimated Bills
When actual meter reading is unavailable, the utility may issue an estimated bill based on the customer’s prior usage. If the customer disputes an estimated bill, the utility must perform an actual reading within 10 business days. If the actual reading shows usage lower than the estimate, the utility will rebill at the actual usage. If the actual reading shows usage higher, the estimated bill stands.

Section 7.1 – Payment Plans
Customers with a proven billing error may request a payment plan for the corrected amount. Requests must be made within 30 days of the corrected bill. Late fees will be waived on the disputed portion if the error is confirmed.

CASE FACTS
Customer: Maria Delgado, account # 558-221-9903, service address 4127 Maple Court, Riverton.
Billing period: March 2024 (period 03/01–03/31).

On April 3, 2024, Maria received a bill for $312.45 for March, of which $198.20 was for electricity (1,482 kWh) and $114.25 for water/sewer (8,500 gallons). Her average electricity use for the prior six months was 920 kWh/month. She called customer service on April 5, 2024, and spoke with agent “Trent.” Trent noted the account and told her an “estimated reading” was used because the meter reader could not access the property due to a locked gate on March 28, 2024. He advised her to submit a written dispute.

On April 8, 2024, Maria emailed a written dispute: “I dispute the entire March bill. My gate was not locked. I was home on March 28. I think the meter is faulty. Please test it.”

On April 9, 2024, a utility technician, Jamal Rivers, visited and performed an actual meter reading. The meter read 45,302 kWh. The previous actual read on February 28, 2024, was 43,820 kWh. The difference is 1,482 kWh, exactly matching the March bill usage. Jamal also visually inspected the meter and noted “no signs of tampering or malfunction.” He did not perform a full meter accuracy test.

On April 10, 2024, customer service replied: “We have verified the actual reading. Your usage is correct. No adjustment.”

On April 12, 2024, Maria submitted a second written request: “I want a formal meter test. I still believe the meter is faulty. My neighbor’s usage is half mine. Also, I want a payment plan for the disputed amount.”

On April 15, 2024, the utility responded: “A formal meter test was not performed on April 9. We will schedule a test within 15 business days.”

On April 18, 2024, the utility performed a full meter accuracy test. Results: meter registered 1.8% fast. The acceptable range is ±2%. The meter was not replaced.

On April 22, 2024, Maria received a corrected bill for March: $312.45 unchanged, because 1.8% is within the acceptable range. No adjustment was made.

On April 25, 2024, Maria called again: “You said you would adjust if the meter was faulty. It was 1.8% fast. That is faulty to me. I want the bill reduced. I also want a payment plan.”

On April 28, 2024, the utility replied: “The meter is within acceptable limits. No billing adjustment. Payment plan not available because no billing error was confirmed.”

DOCUMENTO DE POLÍTICA INTERNA: CONSENTIMENTO PARA MARKETING DIGITAL (LGPD)
Versão 4.2 | Aprovada em: 10/05/2023
Responsável: DPO – Carlos Mendes

CLÁUSULA 1: DEFINIÇÃO DE CONSENTIMENTO VÁLIDO
O consentimento é válido somente se for livre, informado, inequívoco e específico para uma finalidade determinada. Não constitui consentimento a inércia do titular ou a presunção de aceitação.

CLÁUSULA 2: REGISTRO E PROVA
A empresa deve manter registro detalhado da data, hora, IP e conteúdo exato apresentado ao usuário no momento do clique. Registros sem metadados completos são considerados nulos para fins de prova legal.

CLÁUSULA 3: FINALIDADES ESPECÍFICAS
Cada canal (e-mail, SMS, WhatsApp) e cada tipo de conteúdo (transacional, promocional, curadoria editorial) exige opt-in separado. A seleção de "Aceito receber novidades" não autoriza envio de ofertas comerciais agressivas ou descontos exclusivos, salvo se o texto do checkbox mencionasse explicitamente "ofertas e promoções".

From: Sarah Jenkins, Logistics Manager
To: Compliance Team
Date: October 12, 2023
Subject: Urgent review required for electronics import from Shenzhen.

Context:
We are currently holding shipment #GL-89204 at the Port of Los Angeles. The cargo consists of 500 units of "SmartHome Hub" devices (HS Code 8517.62). The declared value on the Commercial Invoice is $45,000 USD. However, our internal purchase order (PO #102-B) lists a total cost of $52,000 USD due to expedited freight charges included in the unit price by the supplier, TechNova Solutions.

Customs Broker Report (Oct 11, 2023):
The broker flagged a discrepancy between the invoice value ($45k) and the payment wire transfer ($52k). They requested proof that the $7k difference represents non-dutiable costs (e.g., international freight/insurance incurred outside the US). Per US CBP regulations, if freight/insurance is prepaid by the seller and included in the FOB price but not separated on the invoice, it may be considered part of the dutiable value unless substantiated otherwise.

Supplier Email Thread:
TechNova Rep (Li Wei): "The $45,000 invoice reflects only the manufacturing cost. The extra $7,000 paid via wire was for air freight surcharges we arranged because your client demanded speed. We did not list this separately on the commercial invoice as per standard practice for FOB terms where the buyer usually handles local transport, but here we handled the international leg."

Internal Audit Note:
The Incoterms stated on the Bill of Lading are "FOB Shenzhen." Under FOB, risk and cost transfer to the buyer once goods pass the ship's rail. Typically, under FOB, the buyer pays for main carriage. If TechNova paid for main carriage but billed it separately without including it in the invoice value, this might suggest the transaction value excludes freight. However, CBP generally requires that all payments made as a condition of sale be included in the declared value if they relate to the production or sale of the goods, unless specifically exempted (like international transport after entry point). Since the freight was paid before arrival in the US, its treatment is complex.

Current Action Required:
We need to determine if we should file a Post-Summary Correction (PSC) to increase the declared value to $52,000, or provide documentation proving the $7,000 is strictly non-dutiable transportation cost incurred prior to importation which should be excluded from dutiable value. The broker argues that without explicit separation on the original documents, the default assumption is inclusion in dutiable value. The legal team is unsure if the 'condition of sale' argument holds water given the separate wire transfer timing.

criteria.exclude_freight_if_separate: Argue the $7,000 is non-dutiable international transport cost since it was not part of the merchandise price itself.
criteria.include_in_dutiable_value: Declare the full $52,000 as dutiable value because the payment was a condition of the sale and related to bringing goods to the US.
criteria.request_ruling_from_cbp: Pause the clearance indefinitely until a formal binding ruling is issued by US Customs and Border Protection.
criteria.insufficient_information: It is impossible to decide without knowing the specific Incoterms version used (e.g., FOB vs EXW).

criteria.true: The document confirms the buyer paid the carrier directly.
criteria.false: The document does not confirm this; in fact, the email indicates the supplier paid the surcharge.

2. A transferência somente é permitida até 72 horas antes do início do evento, por meio do aplicativo oficial “Vela Norte”, mediante pagamento de taxa de R$ 35,00 por ingresso.
3. O cessionário deve possuir CPF ativo e aceitar os termos no aplicativo no momento da transferência.
4. Exceção 1 – Sócio Vela: assinantes ativos do plano “Sócio Vela” podem realizar até duas transferências por CPF, sem taxa, desde que a solicitação ocorra até 24 horas antes do evento e o cessionário também seja assinante ativo.
5. Exceção 2 – Reembolso do cedente: se o cedente tiver solicitado reembolso integral e este já houver sido concluído, a transferência fica bloqueada, ainda que o prazo da regra geral não tenha expirado.
6. Transferências para menores de 16 anos exigem autorização por escrito do responsável legal anexada no aplicativo até 48 horas antes do evento.
7. Não é permitida transferência de ingressos obtidos por cortesia, imprensa ou meia-entrada estudantil.
8. Em caso de falha técnica comprovada do aplicativo durante o prazo permitido, o organizador pode autorizar transferência manual por e-mail, exclusivamente pelo endereço ingressos@velanorte.com.br, até 12 horas antes do evento.

O aplicativo exibiu a mensagem “transferência indisponível”.

Section 3.1: Severity Classification
All security alerts must be classified into one of four severity levels based on the potential impact to confidentiality, integrity, or availability. The classification is determined by the following matrix:
- CRITICAL: Immediate threat to core infrastructure, confirmed exfiltration of PII/PHI, or compromise of administrative credentials.
- HIGH: Confirmed breach of a single user account with access to sensitive data, or detection of malware on a server hosting production databases.
- MEDIUM: Unconfirmed suspicious activity from a known IP address, policy violation involving non-sensitive internal documents, or failed login attempts exceeding threshold without successful authentication.
- LOW: Informational events, benign false positives, or minor configuration deviations that do not pose an immediate risk.

Section 4.2: Exception Handling for Legacy Systems
Legacy systems designated as "Critical Infrastructure" in the Asset Inventory Database (AID) are exempt from standard real-time blocking policies due to compatibility risks. However, any alert triggered by these systems must undergo manual review within 4 hours. If a legacy system generates an alert matching a pattern previously identified as malicious in the Threat Intelligence Feed (TIF), it must be escalated to CRITICAL regardless of the automatic classifier score. Note: This escalation rule supersedes Section 3.1 for assets explicitly tagged [LEGACY-CRIT].

Note: If an item was certified when purchased but later withdrawn from the catalog due to fraud, it remains eligible if the business can prove no knowledge of the fraud at the time of purchase.
3. USAGE REQUIREMENT: The equipment must be used exclusively for business purposes. Any personal use, however minor, disqualifies the entire deduction for that unit. This rule applies without exception; there is no pro-rated allowance for mixed-use items.
4. COST THRESHOLD: The total invoice amount (including tax) must exceed $5,000 per unit. Items costing $5,000 or less are not eligible for this specific high-tier deduction, though they may qualify for other standard depreciation schedules not covered here.
5. DOCUMENTATION: A valid receipt showing the date, vendor, item description, and certification code is mandatory. Missing documentation results in automatic denial, regardless of the underlying eligibility of the asset.

CASE FILE: Ticket #8942-B
Analyst: David Chen
Client: NovaTech Solutions Inc.
Item Description: High-Efficiency HVAC Unit Model X-700
Invoice Date: March 10, 2024
Total Cost: $12,400 (includes sales tax)
Vendor Status: At the time of purchase (March 10, 2024), the vendor’s catalog listed Model X-700 as "Pending Certification." The certification was officially granted by the regulatory body on April 1, 2024.
Usage Log: Security camera footage from the client’s office confirms the unit operates 24/7. Client statement indicates that during weekends, the facility manager uses the building for a private home gym located in the basement, which shares the same HVAC loop as the main server room. The client argues that the server room usage constitutes 95% of the total operational hours, so only 5% should be disqualified.
Documentation: A scanned invoice is attached. It shows the cost and date. However, the field for "Certification Code" is blank on the invoice itself. The analyst found a separate email from the vendor dated March 15, 2024, stating, "Your order for X-700 is complete. We anticipate final approval shortly."

ANALYST NOTE:
David Chen submitted a preliminary recommendation to approve the full $12,400 deduction, citing the eventual certification and the high percentage of business usage. He argued that since the certification happened within the same fiscal year, it should count retroactively. Regarding the usage, he suggested applying a 95% pro-rata calculation. Please review against the strict policy above.

To: David Chen <dchen@firm.com>
Subject: Re: Ticket #8942-B Review

I’ve reviewed your notes. You need to look closer at Rule 2 and Rule 3. 

Regarding Rule 2: The policy states the item must be listed as "Certified" AT THE TIME OF PURCHASE. Your note says it was "Pending" on March 10. Does "Pending" equal "Certified"? No. The fact that it became certified on April 1 does not change its status on March 10. Unless you have proof the vendor knew it would be certified and mislabeled it, it fails Rule 2. Did you check the "withdrawn/fraud" exception? That doesn't apply here because it wasn't withdrawn; it just wasn't ready yet.

Regarding Rule 3: You mentioned 95% business use. Read Rule 3 again. It says "exclusively for business purposes... any personal use... disqualifies the entire deduction." Is 5% personal use considered "any" use? Yes. Therefore, the argument for pro-rating is invalid under this specific simplified policy. 

However, before you deny it entirely, check Rule 5. Is the missing certification code on the invoice fatal? The policy says "Missing documentation results in automatic denial." But we also have the vendor email. Does the email satisfy the "valid receipt" requirement if the receipt lacks the code? The policy demands the receipt show the code. The email is not the receipt. 

So, we have multiple failures. 
1. Not Certified at Purchase.
2. Mixed Use.
3. Documentation deficiency regarding the code on the primary document.

Wait, let me double-check the definition of "Valid Receipt" in Appendix C (not provided here, assume standard). Usually, supplemental docs can cure minor errors. But Rule 2 is substantive, not documentary. 

Bottom line: Can this claim be approved?

Sarah

1. ELIGIBILITY FOR ETF WAIVER:
Agents may waive the Early Termination Fee (ETF) ONLY IF the customer meets ALL of the following criteria:
   a. The current plan contract has at least 6 months remaining before expiration.
   b. The customer has maintained a perfect payment history for the last 12 consecutive billing cycles.
   c. The downgrade request is made within 30 days of a documented network outage affecting their specific zip code lasting more than 4 hours.
   d. The new plan selected must be part of the "Value Family" tier or higher. Basic plans are ineligible for waivers.

2. PRICING ADJUSTMENTS:
If an ETF waiver is granted, the monthly rate for the new plan remains unchanged from the standard tariff. If no waiver is granted, the customer must pay the full ETF amount ($150 flat fee) plus the first month's pro-rated charge for the new plan.

3. VERIFICATION PROTOCOLS:
All claims regarding network outages must be cross-referenced with the central Network Operations Center (NOC) log ID. Agent notes claiming "customer reported outage" without a NOC ID reference are considered unsubstantiated and do not qualify for waivers.

DOCUMENT 1: POLICY EXCERPT — HAVENPORT FOODS COLD CHAIN & HOT HOLDING POLICY (Rev. 7, effective 2025-03-01)

Section 4.2 Cold Holding: All ready-to-eat (RTE) and raw animal foods held cold must be maintained at or below 41°F (5°C). Temperatures must be recorded at least once every 4 hours during active operation, and at the start of each shift. Corrective action is required immediately if any reading exceeds 41°F.

Section 4.2.1 Corrective Action for Cold Holding Deviations:
(a) If a reading is between 42°F and 45°F and the food has been held for less than 4 hours above 41°F, the food may be rapidly cooled to 41°F or below and retained for service.
(b) If a reading is above 45°F, or if the food has been above 41°F for 4 hours or more, the food must be discarded.
(c) If time-above-41°F cannot be determined, the food must be discarded.

Section 4.3 Hot Holding: All hot-held TCS foods must be maintained at or above 135°F (57°C). Temperatures must be recorded at least once every 2 hours. Corrective action is required immediately if any reading is below 135°F.

Section 4.3.1 Corrective Action for Hot Holding Deviations:
(a) If a reading is between 130°F and 134°F and the food has been held below 135°F for less than 2 hours, the food may be reheated to 165°F for 15 seconds and retained for service.
(b) If a reading is below 130°F, or if the food has been below 135°F for 2 hours or more, the food must be discarded. Reheating is not allowed.
(c) If time-below-135°F cannot be determined, the food must be discarded.

Section 5.1 Recording: All temperature logs must record date, time, food item, measured temperature, initials of the person recording, and any corrective action taken. Missing initials are a documentation deficiency, not a food safety deviation.

Section 5.2 Review: The Person in Charge (PIC) must review logs daily. Any deviation requiring discard triggers a Corrective Action Report (CAR) within 24 hours. Any deviation that is corrected without discard triggers a log note only.

Section 7.0 Escalation: If a discard occurs for more than 5 lbs of protein, or if the same deviation recurs within 7 days, the incident must be escalated to the Regional Food Safety Manager within 24 hours.

FROM: Sarah Jenkins, Regional Quality Assurance Manager
TO: Kitchen Managers, Site B (Downtown)

SUBJECT: Correction of Non-Conformance in Cold Holding Logs

Per company policy SOP-402, all ready-to-eat (RTE) foods held at temperatures below 41°F (5°C) must be checked every two hours. Any temperature reading above 41°F constitutes a critical violation requiring immediate discard and corrective action logging. If a reading is exactly 41.0°F, it is considered compliant for that specific interval but requires increased monitoring frequency for the next four hours.

Case Facts:
On October 10, 2023, the cold holding unit #4 (Chiller Alpha) experienced intermittent compressor failures between 09:00 and 17:00. The automated digital thermometer logs were manually transcribed by Line Cook Marcus Thorne into the paper logbook. Marcus noted that the automatic system failed to record data from 11:00 to 13:00 due to battery depletion. During this gap, Marcus performed manual spot checks using a calibrated stem thermometer.

Log Entry Excerpt:
- 09:00: 38.5°F (Auto)
- 10:00: 39.0°F (Auto)
- 11:00: [MISSING AUTO DATA] - Manual Check: 40.5°F
- 12:00: [MISSING AUTO DATA] - Manual Check: 41.0°F
- 13:00: [MISSING AUTO DATA] - Manual Check: 42.5°F
- 14:00: 43.0°F (Auto resumed)
- 15:00: 42.0°F (Auto)
- 16:00: 40.0°F (Auto)
- 17:00: 39.5°F (Auto)

Note on Product Inventory:
The unit contained three distinct trays of RTE chicken salad prepared on October 9. Tray A was placed in the front-left position, Tray B in the center-back, and Tray C in the front-right. Marcus’s manual checks were taken from the geometric center of the unit, approximately 2 inches away from Tray B, which was sealed with plastic wrap. Trays A and C were uncovered.

Email Thread:
From: David Chen (Site B Manager)
To: Sarah Jenkins
Subject: Re: Chiller Alpha Log
Date: Oct 11, 2023, 08:15 AM
Sarah,
We received your flag regarding the 13:00 reading. We have discarded all inventory as per SOP. However, I am disputing the non-conformance citation for the 12:00 entry. Marcus recorded 41.0°F. Your memo states this is "compliant." Therefore, we should not be penalized for the entire shift, only for the 13:00 breach. Also, did Marcus check Tray A or C specifically? The log doesn't say. He said he checked the "unit," not specific trays. Is that sufficient?

From: Sarah Jenkins
To: David Chen
Subject: Re: Chiller Alpha Log
Date: Oct 11, 2023, 09:30 AM
David,
The 12:00 reading triggers the "increased monitoring" clause, not full compliance exemption. Since no readings were taken between 12:00 and 13:00 other than the single point, we cannot verify if the temperature spiked above 41.0°F in the interim. Regarding tray specifics: SOP-402 Section 3.2 requires product-specific verification when ambient air temperature deviates from standard operating ranges (>40°F). Since the air temp hit 42.5°F, we need proof that the product core temperature remained safe. Marcus’s log does not list core temps for Trays A or C. Without this, the assumption is the worst-case scenario for uncovered products.

TAX YEAR 2024 — SIMPLIFIED DEDUCTION RULES (FICTIONAL)

Section 12.1 — Home Office Deduction. A taxpayer may claim the Home Office Deduction only if they used a portion of their home exclusively and regularly as their principal place of business. The deduction is not available if the taxpayer is an employee and their employer provides a suitable workspace that the employee could use, unless the employee does not use that employer-provided workspace. The deduction is also not available if the taxpayer rented their home and the landlord prohibited business use.

Section 12.2 — Professional Development Deduction. A taxpayer may claim the Professional Development Deduction for costs of courses, certifications, or conferences that maintain or improve skills required in the taxpayer's current trade or business. The deduction is not allowed for expenses that qualify the taxpayer for a new trade or business, even if the new trade is related to the current one. The deduction is disallowed if the taxpayer was reimbursed for the expense and did not include the reimbursement in income.

Section 12.3 — Charitable Mileage Deduction. A taxpayer may claim a deduction for mileage driven in service of a qualified charitable organization at the standard charitable rate of $0.14 per mile. The deduction is not allowed if the taxpayer has already claimed the same mileage as a business expense. The deduction is also disallowed if the taxpayer received a flat car allowance from the charity that was intended to cover vehicle costs, regardless of whether the allowance was reported as income.

Section 12.4 — Dependent Care Credit (not a deduction, but treated here for simplification). A taxpayer may claim the Dependent Care Credit for expenses paid for the care of a qualifying dependent so the taxpayer could work. The credit is not available if the taxpayer files as Married Filing Separately, unless the taxpayer lived apart from their spouse for the last 6 months of the year. The credit is reduced if the taxpayer's adjusted gross income exceeds $50,000.

DOCUMENT: Municipal Code Section 14.2.030 - Residential Addition Permit Requirements (Excerpt)
Effective Date: January 1, 2023
Applicability: Single-family residential properties in Zones R-1 through R-4.

A permit application for a residential addition is considered 'Complete' and eligible for expedited review only if ALL of the following conditions are met simultaneously:
1. The proposed addition does not increase the existing structure's footprint by more than 50% or 1,000 square feet, whichever is less.
2. All architectural drawings must be stamped by a licensed professional engineer OR an architect registered in this state. A draftsperson’s signature alone is insufficient unless accompanied by a letter of intent from a licensed professional assuming responsibility.
3. Site plans must clearly indicate setbacks. If any setback is reduced below the standard minimum (Front: 15ft, Side: 5ft, Rear: 20ft), a variance request form (Form V-99) MUST be attached to the application package at the time of submission. Applications submitted without Form V-99 where variances are required will be deemed 'Incomplete' and rejected.
4. Proof of property ownership must include either a current title report issued within the last 60 days OR a notarized deed recorded with the county clerk prior to the date of application submission.
5. There shall be no outstanding code violations on the subject property as of the application date.

Subject: Clarification on Visa Chargeback Rules for 'Goods Not Received' (Code 13.1)

Effective immediately, the following rules apply to all disputes filed under Reason Code 13.1 (Cardholder Claims Goods or Services Not Received):

1. Eligibility Window: A chargeback may only be initiated if the transaction date is within 120 days of the dispute filing date. This window starts from the date the goods were supposed to arrive, not the purchase date.
2. Documentation Requirement: The cardholder must provide a written request for cancellation/refund sent to the merchant at least 15 calendar days prior to filing the chargeback. Proof of this email/message must be attached to the ticket.
3. Merchant Response Time: Merchants have 30 days to respond to the initial retrieval request. If they do not respond, the chargeback proceeds automatically unless the cardholder’s documentation is incomplete.
4. Exclusion Clause: Chargebacks are strictly prohibited for digital goods delivered instantly via email link, provided the merchant can prove delivery logs. Physical items shipped with tracking marked 'Delivered' require a police report if claimed stolen after delivery.

CONTROLE DE QUALIDADE – PROCEDIMENTO DE BLOQUEIO E LIBERAÇÃO DE LOTE

Código: PQ-07 Revisão: 4 Data de vigência: 02/01/2025

1. OBJETIVO
Estabelecer critérios para bloqueio, avaliação e liberação de lotes manufaturados na Planta Industrial Vale Verde Ltda. (CNPJ 12.345.678/0001-90), unidade de Contagem/MG.

2. DEFINIÇÕES
2.1 Lote: conjunto de unidades produzidas sob as mesmas condições e registradas no sistema MES sob um número único.
2.2 Bloqueio: status que impede a expedição do lote até decisão formal da Qualidade.
2.3 Liberação: autorização formal para expedição, uso ou retrabalho.
2.4 Desvio Crítico: não conformidade que afeta segurança, eficácia ou requisito regulatório do produto.
2.5 Desvio Maior: não conformidade que afeta função ou desempenho, mas não é crítica.
2.6 Desvio Menor: não conformidade que não afeta função, segurança ou regulamento.

3. REGRAS GERAIS
3.1 Todo lote com desvio classificado como Crítico deve ser rejeitado (scrap), não sendo permitida liberação condicional.
3.2 Todo lote com desvio classificado como Maior deve ser bloqueado e submetido a disposição pela Qualidade.
3.3 Todo lote com desvio classificado como Menor pode ser liberado sob concessão, desde que aprovado pelo Gerente da Qualidade.
3.4 A liberação de qualquer lote bloqueado exige parecer técnico da Engenharia de Qualidade e aprovação final do Gerente da Qualidade.
3.5 Amostragem de inspeção final: para lotes de até 500 unidades, inspecionar 32 unidades; para lotes de 501 a 3.200 unidades, inspecionar 125 unidades; acima de 3.200, inspecionar 200 unidades.
3.6 O lote deve permanecer bloqueado no MES até que a Qualidade registre a decisão final no ticket correspondente.

4. EXCEÇÃO – CLÁUSULA 4.1
Um lote com desvio Crítico pode ser retrabalhado e liberado somente se todas as condições a seguir forem atendidas cumulativamente:
(a) o desvio crítico for detectado antes da expedição;
(b) houver procedimento de retrabalho validado e aprovado pela Engenharia de Qualidade;
(c) o retrabalho for executado por operadores certificados;
(d) após o retrabalho, 100% das unidades do lote forem reinspecionadas quanto ao requisito afetado;
(e) a reinspeção não encontrar nenhuma unidade não conforme;
(f) o Gerente da Qualidade e o Diretor Industrial aprovarem formalmente a liberação.
Se qualquer condição não for atendida, o lote deve ser rejeitado (scrap).

- IT-12 Instrução de Retrabalho de Vedações
- FT-09 Ficha de Inspeção Final

SECTION 3: LOCAL TRANSPORTATION AND PARKING
3.1 Ground Transportation: Employees are reimbursed for reasonable local transportation costs when incurred in the course of business travel or during extended workdays exceeding 12 hours.
